title.zh: 卷一百五十七 志第一百一十 選舉三
title.en: Volume 157 Treatises 110: Selection and Appointment of Officials 3
title.raw: 卷一百五十七 志第一百一十 選舉三 Volume 157 Treatises 110: Selection and Appointment of Officials 3

sentences.zh: 選舉三

translations.literal: Selection and Appointment 3
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Appointment of Officials, Part Three

sentences.zh: 〈（學校試律學等試附）〉

translations.literal: (Appended: school examinations, law-school examinations, and related examinations)
translations.idiomatic: (With appended material on school examinations, law-school examinations, and related tests)

sentences.zh: 凡學皆隸國子監。

translations.literal: As a rule, all schools were subordinate to the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In general, every school fell under the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 國子生，以京朝七品以上子孫為之，初無定員，後以二百人為額。

translations.literal: Students of the Directorate were drawn from descendants of capital officials of the seventh rank and above; at first there was no fixed quota, but later the quota was set at two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students were recruited from the descendants of metropolitan officials of the seventh rank and above. There was initially no fixed quota; later it was set at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 太學生，以八品以下子弟若庶人之俊異者為之。

translations.literal: Imperial College students were drawn from sons of officials below the eighth rank, or from commoners of outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College students came from the sons of officials below the eighth rank, or from exceptionally gifted commoners.

sentences.zh: 及三舍法行，則太學始定置外舍生二千人，內舍生三百人，上舍生百人。

translations.literal: When the Three-Hall system was implemented, the Imperial College first fixed quotas of two thousand outer-hall students, three hundred inner-hall students, and one hundred upper-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Three-Hall system took effect, the Imperial College established fixed quotas of two thousand outer-hall students, three hundred inner-hall students, and one hundred upper-hall students.

sentences.zh: 始入學，驗所隸州公據，試補外舍，齋長、諭月書其行藝於籍。

translations.literal: On first entering study, one verified the official certificate from one's home prefecture, was examined for placement in the outer hall, and the hall chief and instructor recorded conduct and achievement in the register each month.
translations.idiomatic: On first enrollment, students presented the official certificate from their home prefecture, sat an examination for placement in the outer hall, and each month the hall chief and instructor recorded their conduct and academic performance in the register.

sentences.zh: 行謂率教不戾規矩，藝謂治經程文。

translations.literal: "Conduct" meant following instruction without violating rules; "achievement" meant mastery of the classics and examination compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct meant obeying instruction without breaking regulations; achievement meant proficiency in the classics and in examination essays.

sentences.zh: 季終考於學諭，次學錄，次正，次博士，後考於長貳。

translations.literal: At the end of each season they were examined by the instructor, then the recorder, then the director, then the erudite, and finally by the chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of each season students were examined in turn by the instructor, the recorder, the director, the erudite, and finally the senior administrators.

sentences.zh: 歲終會其高下，書於籍，以俟復試，參驗而序進之。

translations.literal: At year's end their standings were tallied and entered in the register, to await re-examination; after cross-checking, they were advanced in order.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end their rankings were compiled and recorded, pending re-examination; after verification, students were promoted in sequence.

sentences.zh: 凡私試，孟月經義，仲月論，季月策。

translations.literal: For private examinations: in the first month of the season, exposition of the classics; in the middle month, discourse; in the last month, policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Private examinations were held as follows: in the first month of each season, exposition of the classics; in the middle month, discursive essays; in the last month, policy questions.

sentences.zh: 凡公試，初場經義，次場論策。

translations.literal: For public examinations: the first session tested exposition of the classics; the second, discourse and policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Public examinations consisted of a first session on exposition of the classics and a second on discursive essays and policy questions.

sentences.zh: 試上舍，如省試法。

translations.literal: Examinations for the upper hall followed the provincial-examination model.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-hall examinations followed the same procedures as the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 凡內舍，行藝與所試之業俱優，為上舍上等，取旨授官；

translations.literal: For the inner hall, when both conduct-achievement and the subject examined were excellent, this counted as upper grade of the upper hall, and an imperial order granted office;
translations.idiomatic: For inner-hall students, if both conduct-achievement and examination performance were excellent, they ranked in the upper grade of the upper hall and received appointment by imperial order;

sentences.zh: 一優一平為中等，以俟殿試；

translations.literal: one excellent and one fair counted as middle grade, awaiting the palace examination;
translations.idiomatic: one excellent and one fair counted as the middle grade and qualified them to await the palace examination;

sentences.zh: 俱平若一優一否為下等，以俟省試。

translations.literal: both fair, or one excellent and one failing, counted as lower grade, awaiting the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: both fair, or one excellent and one failing, counted as the lower grade and qualified them to await the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 元祐間，置廣文館生二千四百人，以待四方遊士試京師者。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era, two thousand four hundred students of the Broad Learning Hall were established to accommodate traveling scholars from all quarters who came to the capital to sit examinations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou period, two thousand four hundred Broad Learning Hall places were created for scholars from all regions who came to the capital to take examinations.

sentences.zh: 律學生無定員，他雜學廢置無常。

translations.literal: Law-school students had no fixed quota; other miscellaneous schools were abolished or restored without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Law-school enrollment had no fixed quota, and other specialized schools were established or abolished at irregular intervals.

sentences.zh: 崇寧建辟雍於郊，以處貢士，而三舍考選法乃遍天下。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era the Bright Hall was built in the suburbs to house presented scholars, and the Three-Hall examination-and-selection system then spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning, the Bright Hall was built in the suburbs to house presented scholars, and the Three-Hall examination and selection system was extended empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 於是由州郡貢之辟雍，由辟雍升之太學，而學校之制益詳。

translations.literal: Thereupon prefectures and commanderies presented scholars to the Bright Hall, and from the Bright Hall they advanced to the Imperial College, and the school system grew ever more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter prefectures and commanderies presented scholars to the Bright Hall, and from the Bright Hall they advanced to the Imperial College, and the school system became increasingly elaborate.

sentences.zh: 凡國子以奏蔭恩廣，故學校不預考選，其得入官賜出身者，多由銓試。

translations.literal: Directorate students generally entered through memorialized privilege by descent, so schools did not participate in examination selection; those who gained office or granted status mostly did so through selection examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students generally entered through hereditary privilege, so they did not take part in school-based selection; most who received office or granted status did so through the regular selection examinations.

sentences.zh: 初，國子監因周舊制，頗增學舍，以應蔭子孫隸學受業。

translations.literal: At first the Directorate of Education, following the old Zhou system, greatly increased school buildings to accommodate descendants entering by privilege who were registered for study.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Directorate of Education, following the old Zhou model, greatly expanded its buildings to accommodate privileged descendants registered for instruction.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，國子監上言：「生徒舊數七十人，奉詔分習《五經》，然係籍者或久不至，而在京進士、諸科，常赴講席肄業，請以補監生之闕。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao, the Directorate memorialized: "The old number of students was seventy; by imperial order they were divided to study the 《Five Classics》, yet those on the register sometimes did not come for long periods, while metropolitan jinshi and candidates of other categories in the capital regularly attended lectures to pursue study—please allow them to fill vacancies among Directorate students."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 8, the Directorate reported: "The former enrollment was seventy students, assigned by edict to study the 《Five Classics》, yet registered students often stayed away for long periods, while metropolitan degree-holders and candidates of other categories regularly attended lectures. We request that they be allowed to fill vacancies among Directorate students."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 景德間，許文武升朝官嫡親附國學取解，而遠鄉久寓京師，其文藝可稱，有本鄉命官保任，監官驗之，亦聽附學充貢。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era, legitimate sons of civil and military court officials of metropolitan rank were permitted to attach to the Directorate to obtain recommendation; and for those from distant districts long resident in the capital whose literary accomplishment was commendable, if a commissioned official of their home district guaranteed them and Directorate officials verified it, they too were allowed to attach for study and candidacy.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, legitimate sons of civil and military metropolitan officials were permitted to attach to the Directorate to obtain recommendation credentials. Scholars from distant regions long resident in the capital whose literary accomplishment was commendable could also attach for study and candidacy if a commissioned official from their home district vouched for them and Directorate officials verified their credentials.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，士之服儒術者不可勝數。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Renzong, scholars devoted to Confucian learning were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong, scholars devoted to Confucian learning were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 即位初，賜兗州學田，已而命藩輔皆得立學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his reign he granted school fields to Yanzhou; shortly afterward he ordered that all frontier prefectures and circuits might establish schools.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign he granted school lands to Yanzhou, and soon ordered that all frontier prefectures and circuits might establish schools.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，詔曰：「儒者通天、地、人之理，明古今治亂之原，可謂博矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli, an edict stated: "Confucian scholars comprehend the principles of Heaven, Earth, and humanity and understand the origins of order and disorder in past and present—this may be called broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 4, an edict declared: "Confucian scholars comprehend the principles of Heaven, Earth, and humanity and understand the origins of order and disorder through the ages. Their learning may truly be called broad.

sentences.zh: 然學者不得騁其說，而有司務先聲病章句以拘牽之，則吾豪雋奇偉之士，何以奮焉？

translations.literal: Yet when scholars cannot freely expound their views, and the authorities insist on prioritizing tonal faults and textual glosses to constrain them, how can our bold, outstanding, and extraordinary men exert themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when scholars cannot freely develop their ideas, and officials insist on prioritizing tonal rules and textual glosses to constrain them, how can our boldest and most gifted men flourish?

sentences.zh: 士有純明樸茂之美，而無斅學養成之法，使與不肖並進，則夫懿德敏行，何以見焉？

translations.literal: When gentlemen possess the beauty of pure clarity and plain solidity yet lack methods of study and cultivation, and are made to advance together with the unworthy, how can excellent virtue and quick conduct be discerned?
translations.idiomatic: When men of pure clarity and plain integrity lack proper methods of study and cultivation, and advance alongside the unworthy, how can excellent virtue and quick conduct ever be recognized?

sentences.zh: 此取士之甚敝，而學者自以為患。

translations.literal: This is a grave defect in selecting gentlemen, and scholars themselves regard it as a hardship.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave defect in recruiting talent, and scholars themselves regard it as a grievance.

sentences.zh: 夫遇人以簿者，不可責其厚也。

translations.literal: When one meets others with a thin ledger, one cannot demand richness from them.
translations.idiomatic: When men are met with meager provision, one cannot demand richness from them.

sentences.zh: 今朕建學興善，以尊子大夫之行；

translations.literal: Now We establish schools and promote goodness to honor the conduct of the gentleman-officials;
translations.idiomatic: Now We establish schools and promote goodness to honor the conduct of scholar-officials;

sentences.zh: 更製革敝，以盡學者之才。

translations.literal: We reform institutions and remove abuses so that scholars may fully display their talents.
translations.idiomatic: We reform institutions and remove abuses so that scholars may fully display their talents.

sentences.zh: 有司其務嚴訓導、精察舉，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Let the authorities earnestly enforce instruction and guidance and carefully conduct selection, to accord with Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let officials earnestly enforce instruction and conduct careful selection, in accord with Our intent.

sentences.zh: 學者其進德修業，無失其時。

translations.literal: Let scholars advance in virtue and cultivate their studies, and not miss their season.
translations.idiomatic: Let scholars advance in virtue and cultivate their studies without missing their proper season.

sentences.zh: 其令州若縣皆立學，本道使者選部屬官為教授，員不足，取於鄉里宿學有道業者。」

translations.literal: Let every prefecture and county establish schools; circuit commissioners shall select subordinate officials as instructors, and where the quota is insufficient, they shall take men of long-standing learning and moral attainment from the countryside."
translations.idiomatic: Let every prefecture and county establish schools. Circuit commissioners shall select subordinate officials as instructors; where quotas are insufficient, they shall recruit men of long-standing learning and moral attainment from the local community."

sentences.zh: 由是州郡奉詔興學，而士有所勸矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon prefectures and commanderies obeyed the edict and established schools, and gentlemen had encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon prefectures and commanderies obeyed the edict and established schools, and scholars found new encouragement.

sentences.zh: 天章閣侍講王洙言：「國子監每科場詔下，許品官子役然試藝，給牒充廣文、太學、律學三館學生，多致千餘。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu, Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, said: "Whenever an edict for the examination cycle was issued, sons of ranked officials were permitted to try their arts and receive certificates as students of the Broad Learning Hall, Imperial College, and Law School—the three halls—often exceeding a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu, academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, reported: "Whenever an examination-cycle edict was issued, sons of ranked officials were permitted to test their arts and receive certificates as students of the Broad Learning Hall, Imperial College, and Law School—often more than a thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 就試試已，則生徒散歸，講官倚席，但為遊寓之所，殊無肄習之法。

translations.literal: Once the examinations were over, students dispersed home, lecturers leaned on their seats, and the halls became merely places of lodging, with no real method of study.
translations.idiomatic: Once examinations ended, students dispersed, lecturers sat idle, and the halls became mere lodging places with no real method of sustained study.

sentences.zh: 居常聽講者，一二十人爾。」

translations.literal: Those who ordinarily attended lectures numbered only a dozen or twenty."
translations.idiomatic: Those who regularly attended lectures numbered only a dozen or twenty."

sentences.zh: 乃限在學滿五百日，舊已嘗充貢者止百日。

translations.literal: A limit was then set of five hundred days in residence; those who had previously served as candidates needed only one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: A requirement was then imposed of five hundred days in residence; those who had previously served as examination candidates needed only one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 本授官會其實，京朝官保任，始預秋試，每十人與解三人。

translations.literal: Their original appointments were checked against fact; metropolitan officials guaranteed them; only then might they enter the autumn examination, with three recommendations granted for every ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Their original appointments were verified, metropolitan officials vouched for them, and only then could they enter the autumn examination, with three recommendations granted for every ten candidates.

sentences.zh: 凡入學授業，月旦即親書到曆。

translations.literal: For all who entered to receive instruction, on the first of each month they personally recorded attendance in the register.
translations.idiomatic: All who entered to receive instruction personally recorded their attendance in the register on the first of each month.

sentences.zh: 如遇私故或疾告、歸寧，皆給假，違程及期月不來參者，去其籍。

translations.literal: If they met private affairs, illness leave, or home leave, leave was granted; those who exceeded the permitted period and did not return within a month had their names struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Leave was granted for private affairs, illness, or visits home; those who exceeded the permitted period and failed to return within a month were struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 後諫官余靖極言非便，遂罷聽讀日限。

translations.literal: Later the remonstrance official Yu Jing strongly argued that this was inconvenient, and the day-limit for attendance was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later the remonstrance official Yu Jing strongly objected, and the residency requirement for attendance was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初立四門學，自八品至庶人子弟充學生，歲一試補。

translations.literal: The Four Gates School was first established; sons from the eighth rank down to commoners served as students, with annual examination for replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Gates School was first established, enrolling sons from the eighth rank down through commoners, with annual examinations for replenishment.

sentences.zh: 差學官鎖宿、彌封校其藝，疏名上聞而後給牒，不中式者仍聽讀，若三試不中，則出之。

translations.literal: School officials were dispatched to seal the quarters, seal the papers, and grade their accomplishment; names were submitted to the throne and certificates issued only afterward; those who failed might still continue study, but if they failed three examinations they were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: School officials sealed the examination quarters, sealed the papers, and graded candidates' work; names were submitted to the throne before certificates were issued. Those who failed might continue study, but after three failures they were expelled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，學廢。

translations.literal: Before long the school was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the school was abolished.

sentences.zh: 時太學之法寬簡，而上之人必求天下賢士，使專教導規矩之事。

translations.literal: At that time the Imperial College regulations were lenient and simple, yet those above insisted on seeking worthy men throughout the realm to devote themselves to instruction in rules and standards.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Imperial College regulations were lenient, yet the court insisted on finding worthy men throughout the realm to devote themselves to teaching rules and standards.

sentences.zh: 安定胡瑗設教蘇、湖間二十餘年，世方尚詞賦，湖學獨立經義治事齋，以敦實學。

translations.literal: Hu Yuan of Anding taught between Suzhou and Huzhou for more than twenty years; the age still prized rhapsodies and fu, but the Huzhou school alone established halls for classical meaning and practical administration to promote solid learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan of Anding taught in the Suzhou-Huzhou region for more than twenty years. While the age still prized rhapsodies and fu, his Huzhou school alone established halls for classical exegesis and practical administration to promote solid learning.

sentences.zh: 皇祐末，召瑗為國子監直講，數年，進天章閣侍講，猶兼學正。

translations.literal: At the end of Huangyou, Yuan was summoned as lecturer of the Directorate; after several years he was promoted to academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, while still holding the post of director of study.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Huangyou, Yuan was summoned as lecturer of the Directorate; after several years he was promoted to academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion while retaining his post as director of study.

sentences.zh: 其初人未信服，謗議蜂起，瑗強力不倦，卒以有立。

translations.literal: At first people did not yet trust him; slander and criticism swarmed like bees, but Yuan pressed on tirelessly and in the end established himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was not widely trusted; criticism swarmed, but Yuan pressed on tirelessly and in the end won acceptance.

sentences.zh: 每公私試罷，掌儀率諸生會於首善，雅樂歌詩，乙夜乃散。

translations.literal: Whenever private or public examinations ended, the master of ceremonies led the students to assemble at the Hall of First Excellence; refined music and songs were performed, and they dispersed only at the second watch of night.
translations.idiomatic: After each private or public examination, the master of ceremonies led students to assemble at the Hall of First Excellence for refined music and poetry, and they did not disperse until the second watch of night.

sentences.zh: 士或不遠數千里來就師之，皆中心悅服。

translations.literal: Some gentlemen came from several thousand li away to study under him, and all were inwardly pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some scholars traveled thousands of li to study under him, and all were inwardly devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 有司請下湖學，取其法以教太學。

translations.literal: The authorities requested that the Huzhou school's methods be adopted to teach the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities requested that the Huzhou school's methods be adopted for teaching at the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 神宗尤垂意儒學，自京師至郡縣，既皆有學。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong especially devoted attention to Confucian learning; from the capital to prefectures and counties, schools were already established everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong especially devoted attention to Confucian learning, and schools had been established from the capital down to prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 歲時月各有試，程其藝能，以差次升舍，其最優者為上舍，免發解及禮部試而特賜之第。

translations.literal: Each year, season, and month had its examinations; accomplishment was graded and students advanced hall by hall in order; the most excellent became upper-hall students, exempt from prefectural recommendation and Ministry of Rites examination and specially granted a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations were held throughout the year; students were graded and promoted hall by hall, and the most excellent became upper-hall students, exempt from prefectural recommendation and Ministry of Rites examinations and specially granted degrees.

sentences.zh: 遂專以此取士。

translations.literal: Thereupon gentlemen were recruited exclusively by this means.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter recruitment of officials relied exclusively on this system.

sentences.zh: 太學生員，慶曆嘗置內舍生二百人。

translations.literal: Imperial College enrollment: in Qingli two hundred inner-hall students had once been established.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College enrollment: during Qingli, two hundred inner-hall places had been established.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，又增百人，尋詔通額為九百人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining another hundred were added; shortly an edict fixed the total quota at nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining another hundred were added; soon an edict fixed the total quota at nine hundred.

sentences.zh: 四年，盡以錫慶院及朝集院西廡建講書堂四，諸生齋舍、掌事者直廬始僅足用。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, four lecture halls were built entirely from the Xiqing Courtyard and the western wing of the Chaoji Courtyard; student dormitories and quarters for clerks finally barely sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, four lecture halls were built using the Xiqing Courtyard and the western wing of the Chaoji Courtyard; student dormitories and staff quarters finally barely met demand.

sentences.zh: 自主判官外，增置直講為十員，率二員共講一經，令中書遴選，或主判官奏舉。

translations.literal: Apart from the chief administrator, ten lecturers were added, generally two jointly lecturing on one classic; the Secretariat was ordered to select them, or the chief administrator might recommend them by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the chief administrator, ten lecturers were added, generally two jointly lecturing on one classic. The Secretariat was to select them, or the chief administrator might recommend candidates by memorial.

sentences.zh: 生員厘為三等：始入學為外舍，初不限員，後定額七百人；

translations.literal: Students were divided into three grades: on first entering they were outer hall; at first there was no quota limit, later fixed at seven hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Students were divided into three grades: on first entering they were outer-hall students; initially there was no quota, later fixed at seven hundred;

sentences.zh: 外舍升內舍，員二百；

translations.literal: from outer hall to inner hall, quota two hundred;
translations.idiomatic: promotion from outer to inner hall, quota two hundred;

sentences.zh: 內舍升上舍，員百。

translations.literal: from inner hall to upper hall, quota one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: promotion from inner to upper hall, quota one hundred.

sentences.zh: 各執一經，從所講官受學，月考試其業，優等上之中書。

translations.literal: Each held to one classic and received instruction from the lecturer assigned to it; monthly their work was examined, and the excellent were reported to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Each specialized in one classic and studied under its assigned lecturer; monthly examinations were held, and excellent students were reported to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其正、錄、學諭，以上舍生為之，經各二員；

translations.literal: Directors, recorders, and instructors were drawn from upper-hall students, two for each classic;
translations.idiomatic: Directors, recorders, and instructors were drawn from upper-hall students, two per classic;

sentences.zh: 學行卓異者，主判、直講復薦之中書，奏除官。

translations.literal: those of outstanding learning and conduct were again recommended by the chief administrator and lecturers to the Secretariat, which memorialized for appointment to office.
translations.idiomatic: those of outstanding learning and conduct were again recommended by the chief administrator and lecturers to the Secretariat for appointment to office.

sentences.zh: 始命諸州置學官，率給田十頃贍士。

translations.literal: School officials were first ordered established in all prefectures, generally with ten qing of fields granted to support students.
translations.idiomatic: School officials were first ordered established in all prefectures, generally with ten qing of fields granted to support students.

sentences.zh: 初置小學教授。

translations.literal: Elementary-school instructors were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary-school instructors were first established.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂王安石曰：「今談經者人人殊，何以一道德？

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Wang Anshi: "Today those who discourse on the classics all differ from one another—how can morality be unified?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Wang Anshi: "Today those who expound the classics all differ from one another. How can moral teaching be unified?

sentences.zh: 卿所著經，其以頒行，使學者歸一。」

translations.literal: The classics you have authored—issue them for circulation so that scholars may return to unity."
translations.idiomatic: Issue the classics you have authored so that scholars may return to a single standard."

sentences.zh: 八年，頒王安石《書》、《詩》、《周禮義》於學官，是名《三經新義》。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Wang Anshi's 《Exegesis of the Documents》, 《Exegesis of the Odes》, and 《Exegesis of the Rites of Zhou》 were issued to school officials; this was called the 《New Exegeses of the Three Classics》.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Wang Anshi's 《Exegesis of the Documents》, 《Exegesis of the Odes》, and 《Exegesis of the Rites of Zhou》 were issued to school officials under the title 《New Exegeses of the Three Classics》.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，頒《學令》：太學置八十齋，齋各五楹，容三十人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the 《School Regulations》 were issued: the Imperial College established eighty halls, each of five bays, holding thirty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the 《School Regulations》 were issued: the Imperial College established eighty halls, each of five bays and holding thirty students.

sentences.zh: 外舍生二千人，內舍生三百人，上舍生百人。

translations.literal: Outer-hall students two thousand, inner-hall three hundred, upper-hall one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: There were two thousand outer-hall students, three hundred inner-hall students, and one hundred upper-hall students.

sentences.zh: 月一私試，歲一公試，補內舍生；

translations.literal: Monthly one private examination, yearly one public examination, to replenish inner-hall students;
translations.idiomatic: Monthly private examinations and annual public examinations replenished inner-hall students;

sentences.zh: 間歲一舍試，補上舍生，彌封、謄錄如貢舉法；

translations.literal: every other year one hall examination to replenish upper-hall students, with sealed papers and transcription as in the presented-candidate law;
translations.idiomatic: every other year a hall examination replenished upper-hall students, with sealed papers and transcription following presented-candidate procedures;

sentences.zh: 而上舍試則學官不預考校。

translations.literal: but for upper-hall examinations school officials did not participate in grading.
translations.idiomatic: but for upper-hall examinations school officials did not participate in grading.

sentences.zh: 公試，外舍生入第一、第二等，升內舍；

translations.literal: In public examinations, outer-hall students entering the first or second grade were promoted to the inner hall;
translations.idiomatic: In public examinations, outer-hall students who placed in the first or second grade were promoted to the inner hall;

sentences.zh: 內舍生試入優、平二等，升上舍：皆參考所書行藝乃升。

translations.literal: inner-hall students placing in excellent or fair grades were promoted to the upper hall—all promotions referenced recorded conduct and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: inner-hall students who placed in the excellent or fair grades were promoted to the upper hall—all promotions required reference to recorded conduct and achievement.

sentences.zh: 上舍分三等。

translations.literal: The upper hall was divided into three grades.
translations.idiomatic: The upper hall was divided into three grades.

sentences.zh: 學正增為五人，學錄增為十人，學錄參以學生為之。

translations.literal: Directors of study were increased to five, recorders to ten, and recorders were partly drawn from students.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of study were increased to five and recorders to ten; some recorders were drawn from among the students.

sentences.zh: 歲賜緡錢至二萬五千，又取郡縣田租、屋課、息錢之類，增為學費。

translations.literal: Annual grants of cash strings reached twenty-five thousand; moreover prefectural and county land rent, building levies, interest funds, and the like were taken to augment school expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Annual cash grants reached twenty-five thousand strings; prefectural and county land rents, building levies, interest funds, and similar revenues were also allocated to augment school expenses.

sentences.zh: 初，以國子名監，而實未嘗教養國子。

translations.literal: At first it was called the Directorate of the Sons of the State, yet in fact it had never nurtured the sons of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Although it was called the Directorate of the Sons of the State, in fact it had never truly nurtured them.

sentences.zh: 詔許清要官親戚入監聽讀，額二百人，仍盡以開封府解額歸太學，其國子生解額，以太學分數取之，毋過四十人。

translations.literal: An edict permitted relatives of eminent officials to enter the Directorate to attend lectures, quota two hundred; all Kaifeng recommendation quotas were returned to the Imperial College; Directorate student recommendation quotas were taken from Imperial College places, not exceeding forty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted relatives of eminent officials to enter the Directorate to attend lectures, with a quota of two hundred. All Kaifeng recommendation quotas were transferred to the Imperial College; Directorate student quotas were drawn from Imperial College places, not exceeding forty.

sentences.zh: 哲宗時，初置在京小學，曰：「就傅」、「初筮」，凡兩齋。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhezong, an elementary school in the capital was first established, with two halls called "Approaching the Tutor" and "First Divination."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhezong, an elementary school was first established in the capital with two halls called "Approaching the Tutor" and "First Divination."

sentences.zh: 復取太學額百人還開封府。

translations.literal: One hundred Imperial College places were again returned to Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred Imperial College places were returned to Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，開封解額稍優，四方士子多冒畿縣戶，又隸太學不及一年不該解試者，亦往往冒戶。

translations.literal: Previously Kaifeng's recommendation quota had been somewhat generous; scholars from all quarters often falsely registered in metropolitan county households, and those registered at the Imperial College for less than a year who were not eligible for recommendation also often falsely registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Kaifeng's recommendation quota had been relatively generous; scholars from all regions often falsely registered in metropolitan county households, and those registered at the Imperial College for less than a year who were ineligible for recommendation also frequently did so.

sentences.zh: 禮部按舊制，凡試國子監者，先補中廣文館生，乃投牒求試。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites followed the old system: all who tested at the Directorate first had to be placed in the Broad Learning Hall before submitting petitions to seek examination.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites followed the old system: all who tested at the Directorate first had to be placed in the Broad Learning Hall before submitting petitions to seek examination.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，遂依仿其法，立廣文館生。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou, its method was imitated and Broad Learning Hall students were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 7, this method was imitated and Broad Learning Hall places were established.

sentences.zh: 惟開封府元解百人許自試，其嘗取諸科二百、國子額四十者，皆以為本館解額。

translations.literal: Only Kaifeng Prefecture's original quota of one hundred was permitted self-examination; the two hundred formerly taken from various categories and the forty Directorate places were all counted as this hall's recommendation quota.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kaifeng Prefecture's original quota of one hundred was permitted to test independently; the two hundred formerly taken from various categories and the forty Directorate places were all counted as the hall's recommendation quota.

sentences.zh: 遇貢舉年試補館生，中者執牒詣國子監驗試，凡試者十人取一，開封考取亦如之。

translations.literal: In years of presented candidacy, hall students were examined for replenishment; those who passed took certificates to the Directorate for verification examination, one selected for every ten who tested; Kaifeng selection followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: In examination years, hall students were tested for replenishment; those who passed took certificates to the Directorate for verification, with one selected for every ten candidates. Kaifeng selection followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，罷廣文館，其額悉復還之開封府、國子監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing the Broad Learning Hall was abolished and its quotas entirely restored to Kaifeng Prefecture and the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1, the Broad Learning Hall was abolished and its quotas entirely restored to Kaifeng Prefecture and the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 元祐新令，罷推恩之制。

translations.literal: The new regulations of Yuanyou abolished the system of conferred favor.
translations.idiomatic: The new Yuanyou regulations abolished the system of conferred favor.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，監察御史郭知章言：「先帝立三舍法，以歲月稽其行實，故入上舍而中上等者，得不經禮部試，特命以官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Supervising Censor Guo Zhizhang said: "The late emperor established the Three-Hall system to verify conduct and achievement over months and years; therefore those who entered the upper hall and placed in the upper grade could skip the Ministry of Rites examination and receive office by special order.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng, Supervising Censor Guo Zhizhang said: "The late emperor established the Three-Hall system to verify conduct and achievement over months and years. Therefore those who entered the upper hall and placed in the upper grade could skip the Ministry of Rites examination and receive office by special order.

sentences.zh: 責備而持久，故其得也難，誘掖激勸，莫善於此。

translations.literal: Requirements were strict and enduring, so attainment was difficult; for guidance and encouragement nothing was better than this.
translations.idiomatic: Requirements were strict and enduring, so attainment was difficult; for guidance and encouragement nothing served better.

sentences.zh: 宜復元豐法，以廣樂育之德。」

translations.literal: The Yuanfeng system should be restored to broaden the virtue of nurturing talent."
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng system should be restored to broaden the court's virtue in nurturing talent."

sentences.zh: 又請三學補外舍生，依元豐令一歲四試。

translations.literal: He also requested that replenishment of outer-hall students in the three schools follow the Yuanfeng order of four examinations per year.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that replenishment of outer-hall students in the three schools follow the Yuanfeng rule of four examinations per year.

sentences.zh: 於是詔：「太學生悉用元豐製推恩，上等即注官者，歲毋過二人；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered: "Imperial College students were all to use the Yuanfeng system's conferred favor; those in the upper grade immediately appointed to office were not to exceed two persons per year;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then declared: "Imperial College students would again receive office under the Yuanfeng system of conferred favor, with no more than two upper-grade appointees registered for office each year;

sentences.zh: 免禮部試者，每舉五人而止；

translations.literal: those exempted from the Ministry of Rites examination were limited to five persons per round;
translations.idiomatic: exemptions from the Ministry of Rites examination were capped at five per round;

sentences.zh: 免解試者二十人而止。

translations.literal: those exempted from the recommendation examination were limited to twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: exemptions from the recommendation examination were capped at twenty.

sentences.zh: 仍計數對除省試發解額，其元祐法勿用。

translations.literal: Counts were still reckoned against and deducted from metropolitan-examination and recommendation quotas; the Yuanyou method was not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: These numbers were still counted against metropolitan-examination and recommendation quotas, and the Yuanyou rules were abolished.

sentences.zh: 諸三舍升補等法，悉推行舊制。」

translations.literal: All Three-Hall advancement, replenishment, and related regulations were to be fully enforced under the old system."
translations.idiomatic: All Three-Hall rules on advancement and replenishment were to be fully restored under the former system."

sentences.zh: 三年，三省言：「元祐試補太學生不嚴，苟務多取，後試者無闕可撥，宜遵元豐初製，雖在籍生亦重試。」

translations.literal: In the third year, the Three Departments reported: "Yuanyou placement examinations for Imperial College students were not strict; in seeking to take too many, later examinees had no vacancies to be assigned; the early Yuanfeng system should be followed, and even registered students should be re-examined."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 3, the Three Departments reported: "Yuanyou placement exams for Imperial College students had been too lax. In taking too many candidates, later examinees were left without vacancies. The early Yuanfeng system should be restored, and even students already on the register should be re-examined."

sentences.zh: 乃詔在籍生再試，許取三分，創求補者半之；

translations.literal: An edict then ordered re-examination of registered students, permitting selection of three-tenths; for new applicants seeking placement, half that rate was allowed;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required registered students to be re-examined, with thirty percent permitted to pass; for new applicants seeking placement, the pass rate was set at half that;

sentences.zh: 惟上舍生及是年充貢員內舍、外舍先自元豐補入者免再試，餘非再試而中者皆降舍。

translations.literal: Only upper-hall students and inner-hall and outer-hall students filling that year's presentation quota who had originally entered under Yuanfeng placement were exempt from re-examination; all others who passed without re-examination were demoted in hall.
translations.idiomatic: Only upper-hall students and inner- and outer-hall students filling that year's presentation quota who had originally entered under Yuanfeng rules were exempt from re-examination. All others who passed without re-examination were demoted to a lower hall.

sentences.zh: 蔡京上所修《內外學製》，始頒諸天下。

translations.literal: Cai Jing submitted the 《Regulations for Inner and Outer Schools》 he had compiled, and it was first promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing submitted the 《Regulations for Inner and Outer Schools》 he had compiled, and it was promulgated throughout the empire for the first time.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，詔許命官補國子生，毋過四十人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, an edict permitted appointed officials to be placed as Directorate students, not exceeding forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1, an edict allowed appointed officials to be placed as Directorate students, with a cap of forty.

sentences.zh: 凡太學試，令優取《二禮》，許占全額之半，而以其半及他經。

translations.literal: For all Imperial College examinations, preference was given to the 《Two Rites》, which were permitted to occupy half the total quota, while the other half went to other classics.
translations.idiomatic: In Imperial College examinations, candidates specializing in the 《Two Rites》 were given preference and allowed to take up half the total quota; the remaining half went to other classics.

sentences.zh: 復置《春秋》博士。

translations.literal: The erudite for the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The post of erudite for the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 二年，初令諸州行三舍法，考選、升補，悉如太學。

translations.literal: In the second year, prefectures were first ordered to implement the Three-Hall system; examination, selection, advancement, and replenishment all followed the Imperial College model.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 2, prefectures were first required to adopt the Three-Hall system, with examination, selection, advancement, and replenishment all following Imperial College practice.

sentences.zh: 州許補上舍一人，內舍二人，歲貢之。

translations.literal: Each prefecture was permitted to replenish one upper-hall student and two inner-hall students, who were presented annually.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture could replenish one upper-hall and two inner-hall student, who were presented to the capital each year.

sentences.zh: 其上舍附太學外舍，試中補內舍生，三試不升舍，遣還其州。

translations.literal: Their upper-hall students attached to the Imperial College outer hall; if they passed examination they were placed as inner-hall students; if after three examinations they did not advance in hall, they were sent back to their prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-hall students from the prefectures were attached to the Imperial College outer hall. Those who passed were placed in the inner hall; after three failed attempts at advancement, they were sent back to their home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其內舍免試，至則補為外舍生。

translations.literal: Their inner-hall students were exempt from examination; upon arrival they were placed as outer-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-hall students from the prefectures were exempt from examination and, upon arrival, were placed directly in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 諸路選監司一員提舉學校，守貳董幹其事。

translations.literal: Each circuit selected one intendant-supervisor to oversee schools; the prefect and vice-prefect directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit appointed one intendant-supervisor to oversee its schools, with the prefect and vice-prefect directing the work.

sentences.zh: 遇補試上、內舍生，選有出身官一人，同教授考選，須彌封、謄錄。

translations.literal: When replenishment examinations were held for upper- and inner-hall students, one official with examination credentials was selected to examine jointly with the professor; sealing and transcription were required.
translations.idiomatic: When replenishment exams were held for upper- and inner-hall students, one official with examination credentials was appointed to examine jointly with the professor, with sealed papers and transcription required.

sentences.zh: 三年，太學試補外舍改用四季，學官自考，不謄錄，仍添試論一場。

translations.literal: In the third year, Imperial College replenishment examinations for the outer hall were changed to four seasons; school officials examined on their own without transcription, and one additional discourse examination was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 3, outer-hall replenishment exams at the Imperial College were changed to four sessions per year. School officials examined candidates themselves without transcription, and a discourse examination was added.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，宰臣請：「天下州縣並置學，州置教授二員，縣亦置小學。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, chief ministers requested: "Schools were to be established in all prefectures and counties throughout the realm; each prefecture was to have two professors, and each county was also to establish an elementary school.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 1, chief ministers requested: "Schools should be established in every prefecture and county in the empire. Each prefecture would have two professors, and each county would also establish an elementary school.

sentences.zh: 縣學生選考升諸州學，州學生每三年貢太學。

translations.literal: County students were selected by examination to advance to prefectural schools; prefectural students were presented to the Imperial College every three years.
translations.idiomatic: County students would advance to prefectural schools through competitive examination, and prefectural students would be presented to the Imperial College every three years.

sentences.zh: 至則附試，別立號。

translations.literal: Upon arrival they sat attached examinations with separate registration numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival they would sit attached examinations under separate registration numbers.

sentences.zh: 考分三等：入上等補上舍，入中等補下等上舍，入下等補內舍，餘居外舍。

translations.literal: Examinations were divided into three grades: upper grade placed in the upper hall, middle grade placed in the lower tier of the upper hall, lower grade placed in the inner hall, and the remainder remained in the outer hall.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations were ranked in three grades: the top tier entered the upper hall, the middle tier entered the lower tier of the upper hall, the bottom tier entered the inner hall, and the rest remained in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 諸州軍解額，各以三分之一充貢士。

translations.literal: The recommendation quotas of all prefectures and military commands were each to use one-third for presented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture and military command was to allocate one-third of its recommendation quota to presented scholars.

sentences.zh: 開封府留五十五額，解土人之不入學者，餘盡均給諸州，以為貢額。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture retained fifty-five quotas to recommend local residents not enrolled in schools; the remainder was evenly distributed among prefectures as presentation quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture kept fifty-five quotas for recommending local residents not enrolled in schools; the rest was evenly distributed among the prefectures as presentation quotas.

sentences.zh: 外官子弟親戚，許入學一年，給牒至太學，用國子生額解試。

translations.literal: Children and relatives of officials serving outside the capital were permitted one year of enrollment, given certificates to proceed to the Imperial College, and allowed to use Directorate-student quotas for recommendation examination.
translations.idiomatic: Children and relatives of officials serving outside the capital were allowed one year of enrollment, issued certificates to proceed to the Imperial College, and permitted to use Directorate-student quotas for the recommendation examination.

sentences.zh: 州給常平或係省田宅充養士費，縣用地利所出及非係省錢。」

translations.literal: Prefectures supplied Ever-Normal Granary funds or centrally administered fields and dwellings to cover student support; counties used local revenue and non-centrally administered funds."
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures funded student support from Ever-Normal Granary funds or centrally administered fields and dwellings; counties drew on local revenue and non-centrally administered funds."

sentences.zh: 三年，始定諸路增養縣學弟子員，大縣五十人，中縣四十人，小縣三十人。

translations.literal: In the third year, quotas for expanded county-school enrollment were first fixed for all circuits: large counties fifty persons, medium counties forty, small counties thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 3, enrollment quotas for expanded county schools were first fixed across all circuits: fifty for large counties, forty for medium counties, and thirty for small counties.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣學生曾經公、私試者復其身，內舍免戶役，上舍仍免借借如官戶法。

translations.literal: All prefectural and county students who had passed public or private examinations were exempt from personal corvée; inner-hall students were exempt from household labor service; upper-hall students remained exempt from levies and assessments as under the official-household law.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county students who had passed public or private examinations were exempt from personal corvée. Inner-hall students were exempt from household labor service, and upper-hall students remained exempt from levies and assessments under the official-household law.

sentences.zh: 命將作少監李誡，即城南門外相地營建外學，是為辟雍。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Office Li Jie was ordered to select a site outside the southern city gate and build the outer academy, which became the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Office Li Jie was ordered to select a site outside the southern city gate and build the outer academy, known as the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 蔡京又奏：「古者國內外皆有學，周成均蓋在邦中，而黨庠、遂序則在國外。

translations.literal: Cai Jing further memorialized: "In antiquity there were schools both within and without the state; the Zhou State Academy was presumably in the capital, while village schools and district schools were outside the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing further memorialized: "In antiquity schools existed both inside and outside the capital. The Zhou State Academy stood within the realm, while village schools and district schools lay beyond it.

sentences.zh: 臣親承聖詔，天下皆興學貢士，即國南郊建外學以受之，俟其行藝中率，然後升諸太學。

translations.literal: Your subject has personally received the sacred edict that schools throughout the realm are to nurture and present scholars; an outer academy is therefore built in the southern suburbs to receive them, and after their conduct and achievement reach standard level they are then advanced to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: I have personally received Your Majesty's edict to establish schools and present scholars throughout the empire. An outer academy is therefore being built in the southern suburbs to receive them, and once their conduct and achievement reach the required standard, they will advance to the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 凡此聖意，悉與古合。

translations.literal: All of this sacred intent entirely accorded with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: All of this imperial design accords entirely with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 今上其所當行者：太學專處上舍、內舍生，而外學則處外舍生。

translations.literal: He now submitted what should be implemented: the Imperial College would exclusively house upper-hall and inner-hall students, while the outer academy would house outer-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: He now submitted the measures to be implemented: the Imperial College would house only upper- and inner-hall students, while the outer academy would house outer-hall students.

sentences.zh: 今貢士盛集，欲增太學上舍至三百人，內舍六百人，外舍三千人。

translations.literal: Now that presented scholars were gathering in great numbers, he wished to increase Imperial College upper-hall students to three hundred, inner-hall to six hundred, and outer-hall to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With presented scholars now gathering in great numbers, he proposed raising Imperial College enrollment to three hundred upper-hall students, six hundred inner-hall students, and three thousand outer-hall students.

sentences.zh: 外學為四講堂、百齋，齋列五楹，一齋可容三十人。

translations.literal: The outer academy had four lecture halls and one hundred dormitory halls; each hall had five bays and could accommodate thirty persons.
translations.idiomatic: The outer academy would have four lecture halls and one hundred dormitory halls, each hall comprising five bays and accommodating thirty students.

sentences.zh: 士初貢至，皆入外學，經試補入上舍、內舍，始得進處太學。

translations.literal: When scholars were first presented and arrived, all entered the outer academy; only after passing examination and placement in the upper or inner hall could they advance to reside in the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars newly presented from the provinces would all enter the outer academy first; only after passing examinations and placement in the upper or inner hall could they advance to the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 太學外舍，亦令出居外學。

translations.literal: Imperial College outer-hall students were also ordered to move out and reside in the outer academy.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College outer-hall students were also required to move out and reside in the outer academy.

sentences.zh: 其敕、令、格、式，悉用太學見製。

translations.literal: Its edicts, orders, regulations, and forms all followed the Imperial College's existing system.
translations.idiomatic: Its edicts, orders, regulations, and forms would all follow the Imperial College's existing system.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒總治學事，外學官屬，司業、丞各一人，稍減太學博士、正、錄員歸外學，仍增博士為十員，正、錄為五員，學生充學諭者十人，直學二人。」

translations.literal: The Chancellor of the Directorate oversaw all academic affairs. For the outer academy's staff there were one Vice Director and one Assistant; some Imperial College erudite, director, and recorder posts were reduced and transferred to the outer academy, while erudites were increased to ten, directors and recorders to five, ten students served as instructors, and two as direct students."
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of the Directorate would oversee all academic affairs. The outer academy would have one Vice Director and one Assistant. Some Imperial College posts of erudite, director, and recorder would be transferred to the outer academy, with erudites increased to ten, directors and recorders to five, ten students serving as instructors, and two as direct students."

sentences.zh: 三舍生皆繇升貢，遂罷國子監補試。

translations.literal: Three-Hall students all came through advancement and presentation, and the Directorate placement examination was therefore abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since Three-Hall students all entered through advancement and presentation, the Directorate placement examination was abolished.

sentences.zh: 又置諸王宮大、小學教授，立考選法，凡奉祠及仕而解官或需次者，悉許入內、外學。

translations.literal: Professors for the great and small schools of the princely palaces were also established and examination-and-selection regulations were drawn up; all holders of sacrificial appointments and those who had left office after service or were awaiting appointment were permitted to enter the inner and outer academies.
translations.idiomatic: Professors were also appointed for the great and small schools of the princely palaces, and examination-and-selection regulations were established. Holders of sacrificial appointments and those who had left office or were awaiting appointment were all permitted to enter the inner and outer academies.

sentences.zh: 任子不係州土，隨所寓入學，仍別齋居處，別號試考。

translations.literal: Sons by office privilege not tied to a native prefecture entered school wherever they resided, yet were housed in separate halls, assigned separate numbers, and examined separately.
translations.idiomatic: Sons by office privilege not tied to a native prefecture could enroll wherever they resided, but were housed in separate halls, assigned separate registration numbers, and examined separately.

sentences.zh: 曾升補三舍生，後從獻助得官，其入學視任子法。

translations.literal: Those who had once advanced as Three-Hall students and later gained office through charitable contribution were treated under the sons-by-privilege law upon re-entering school.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had once advanced as Three-Hall students and later gained office through charitable contribution were subject to the sons-by-privilege rules upon re-enrollment.

sentences.zh: 凡任子，不問文武，須隸學滿一年，始得求試。

translations.literal: All sons by privilege, whether civil or military, had to be enrolled in school for a full year before they could seek examination.
translations.idiomatic: All sons by privilege, civil or military alike, had to remain enrolled in school for a full year before they could sit for examination.

sentences.zh: 乃詔取士悉由學校升貢，其州郡發解及試禮部並罷。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that recruitment of scholars proceed entirely through school advancement and presentation; prefectural recommendation and the Ministry of Rites examination were both abolished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then declared that all recruitment of scholars would proceed through school advancement and presentation, abolishing both prefectural recommendation and the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲試上舍，悉差知舉，如禮部試。

translations.literal: From this time, the annual upper-hall examination had chief examiners appointed for all cases, as in the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, chief examiners were appointed for the annual upper-hall examination, following Ministry of Rites practice.

sentences.zh: 五年，著令：

translations.literal: In the fifth year, regulations were codified:
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 5, regulations were codified:

sentences.zh: 凡縣學生隸學已及三月，不犯上二等罰，聽次年試補州學外舍，是名「歲升」。

translations.literal: All county students enrolled for three months or more who had not incurred penalties of the two highest grades were permitted the following year to sit replenishment examination for the prefectural school outer hall; this was called "annual advancement."
translations.idiomatic: County students enrolled for at least three months without incurring penalties of the two highest grades were permitted the following year to sit the replenishment exam for the prefectural school outer hall. This was called "annual advancement."

sentences.zh: 開封祥符生員，即辟雍別為齋，教養、升進如縣學法。

translations.literal: Students of Xiangfu in Kaifeng were given separate halls in the Bright Hall; nurturing, instruction, and advancement followed county-school regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Students of Xiangfu in Kaifeng were assigned separate halls in the Bright Hall, with nurturing, instruction, and advancement following county-school rules.

sentences.zh: 願入鄰縣學者聽。

translations.literal: Those wishing to enter a neighboring county school were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Students wishing to enroll in a neighboring county school were permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 惟赤縣校試，主以博士。

translations.literal: Only for metropolitan-county school examinations were erudites made chief examiners.
translations.idiomatic: Only metropolitan-county school examinations were administered chiefly by erudites.

sentences.zh: 每歲正月，州以公試上舍及歲升員，一院鎖宿，分為三試。

translations.literal: Each year in the first month, the prefecture gathered upper-hall public-examination candidates and annual-advancement candidates in one sealed compound and divided them into three examination sessions.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the first month, the prefecture gathered upper-hall public-examination candidates and annual-advancement candidates in one sealed compound and divided the examination into three sessions.

sentences.zh: 其公試，上舍率十取其六為中格；

translations.literal: For the public examination, six of every ten upper-hall candidates constituted the passing standard;
translations.idiomatic: In the public examination, six of every ten upper-hall candidates constituted the passing standard;

sentences.zh: 中格已，以其名第自上而下參考察之籍；

translations.literal: once the standard was met, their names and ranks were cross-referenced from top to bottom against the merit-review register;
translations.idiomatic: once that standard was met, their names and ranks were cross-referenced from top to bottom against the merit-review register;

sentences.zh: 既在籍，又中選，即六人之中取其四，以差升舍。

translations.literal: those both on the register and selected then had four taken from every six for differential hall advancement.
translations.idiomatic: those both on the register and selected then had four of every six chosen for differential hall advancement.

sentences.zh: 其歲升中選者，得補外舍生。

translations.literal: Those selected through annual advancement were placed as outer-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: Those selected through annual advancement were placed in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 開封屬縣附辟雍別試，中者入辟雍充外舍。

translations.literal: Counties subordinate to Kaifeng sat attached separate examinations at the Bright Hall; those who passed entered the Bright Hall as outer-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: Counties subordinate to Kaifeng sat separate attached examinations at the Bright Hall; those who passed entered the Bright Hall as outer-hall students.

sentences.zh: 隸學三年，經兩試不預升貢，即除其籍，法涉太嚴。

translations.literal: After three years of enrollment, if one failed to qualify for advancement and presentation in two examinations, one's register entry was removed; the law was overly strict.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of enrollment, students who failed to qualify for advancement and presentation in two examinations were struck from the register; the rule was considered too harsh.

sentences.zh: 今令三年內三經公試不預選，兩經補內舍、貢上舍不及格，且曾犯三等以上罰，若外舍，即除籍罷歸縣，內舍降外舍，已嘗降而私試不入等，若曾犯罰，亦除籍，再赴歲升試。

translations.literal: The new order provided: within three years, if one failed to qualify in three public examinations, or failed twice in inner-hall replenishment or upper-hall presentation, and had incurred penalties of the third grade or above—if in the outer hall, one's register was removed and one was dismissed to the county; if in the inner hall, one was demoted to the outer hall; if already demoted and failing to place in a private examination, or if one had incurred penalties, one's register was also removed and one had to retake the annual-advancement examination.
translations.idiomatic: The new rule provided: within three years, outer-hall students who failed to qualify in three public examinations, or failed twice in inner-hall replenishment or upper-hall presentation and had incurred penalties of the third grade or above, were struck from the register and sent back to their county. Inner-hall students were demoted to the outer hall. Those already demoted who failed to place in a private examination, or who had incurred penalties, were also struck from the register and had to retake the annual-advancement examination.

sentences.zh: 凡州學上舍生升舍，以其秋即貢入辟雍，長吏集闔郡官及提學官，具宴設以禮敦遣，限歲終悉集闕下。

translations.literal: When prefectural upper-hall students advanced in hall, they were presented to the Bright Hall that autumn; the chief administrator gathered all county officials and the school intendant, provided a banquet and sent them off with ceremony, and required all to assemble at the capital by year's end.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural upper-hall students advanced in hall, they were presented to the Bright Hall that autumn. The chief administrator gathered all county officials and the school intendant, hosted a farewell banquet, and required all to reach the capital by year's end.

sentences.zh: 自川、廣、福建入貢者，給借職券，過二千里給大將券，續其路食，皆以學錢給之。

translations.literal: Those presented from Sichuan, Guang, and Fujian were given temporary-rank certificates; beyond two thousand li they were given great-general certificates; travel provisions were continued, all paid from school funds.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholars from Sichuan, Guang, and Fujian were issued temporary-rank certificates; beyond two thousand li they received great-general travel certificates. Travel provisions were supplied throughout, all paid from school funds.

sentences.zh: 如有孝弟、睦姻、任恤、忠和，若行能尤異為鄉里所推，縣上之州，免試入學。

translations.literal: If one displayed filial piety and fraternal duty, harmonious kinship, responsibility, and loyalty and harmony, or if conduct and ability were exceptionally outstanding and recommended by the community, the county reported to the prefecture and one entered school without examination.
translations.idiomatic: Those displaying filial piety and fraternal duty, harmonious kinship, responsibility, and loyalty and harmony, or whose conduct and ability were exceptionally outstanding and recommended by their community, were reported by the county to the prefecture and admitted to school without examination.

sentences.zh: 州守貳若教授詢審無謬，即保任入貢，具實以聞，不實者坐罪有差。

translations.literal: If the prefect, vice-prefect, or professor inquired and found no error, they guaranteed the candidate for presentation and reported the facts; if the report was false, punishment was imposed according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: If the prefect, vice-prefect, or professor verified the facts and found no error, they guaranteed the candidate for presentation and reported accordingly. False reports were punished according to degree.

sentences.zh: 太學試上舍生，本慮與科舉相並，試以間歲。

translations.literal: Imperial College upper-hall examinations had originally been held in alternate years for fear of overlapping with the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College upper-hall examinations had originally been held every other year for fear of conflicting with the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 今既罷科舉，又諸州歲貢士，其改用歲試。

translations.literal: Now that the civil-service examinations had been abolished and prefectures presented scholars annually, the examination was changed to an annual test.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the civil-service examinations had been abolished and prefectures presented scholars each year, the examination was changed to an annual test.

sentences.zh: 每春季，太學、辟雍生悉公試，同院混取，總五百七十四人。

translations.literal: Each spring, Imperial College and Bright Hall students all sat public examinations in one compound with mixed selection, totaling five hundred seventy-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring, Imperial College and Bright Hall students sat public examinations together in one compound, with five hundred seventy-four selected in all.

sentences.zh: 以四十七人為上等，即推恩釋褐；

translations.literal: Forty-seven persons constituted the upper grade and immediately received conferred favor and donned office;
translations.idiomatic: Forty-seven were ranked in the upper grade and immediately received conferred favor and donned official robes;

sentences.zh: 一百四十人為中等，遇親策士許入試；

translations.literal: one hundred forty constituted the middle grade and, when the palace examination with imperial questioning occurred, were permitted to enter the test;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred forty were ranked in the middle grade and, when the palace examination with imperial questioning was held, were permitted to sit for it;

sentences.zh: 一百八十七人為下等，補內舍生。

translations.literal: one hundred eighty-seven constituted the lower grade and were placed as inner-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: one hundred eighty-seven were ranked in the lower grade and were placed in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 凡上等上舍生暨特舉孝弟行能之士，不待廷試推恩者，許即引見釋褐。

translations.literal: All upper-grade upper-hall students and men specially recommended for filial piety, fraternal duty, and ability who did not await palace-examination conferred favor were permitted immediate audience and donning of office.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-grade upper-hall students and men specially recommended for filial piety, fraternal duty, and ability who did not await palace-examination conferred favor were permitted immediate audience and donning of official robes.

sentences.zh: 上舍仍先以試文卷進入，得可乃引賜。

translations.literal: Upper-hall students still first submitted their examination essays for review; only upon approval were they granted audience and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-hall students still had to submit their examination essays for review first; only upon approval were they granted audience and conferred favor.

sentences.zh: 若上舍已該釋褐恩，而貢入在廷試前一年者，須在學又及半年，不犯上二等罰，乃得注官。

translations.literal: If an upper-hall student was already eligible for donning-office favor but was presented in the year before the palace examination, he had to remain in school for another half year without incurring penalties of the two highest grades before he could be appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: If an upper-hall student was already eligible for donning-office favor but was presented in the year before the palace examination, he had to remain in school for another six months without incurring penalties of the two highest grades before he could be registered for office.

sentences.zh: 凡貢士入辟雍外舍，三經試不與升補，兩經試不入等，仍犯上三等罰者，削籍再赴本州歲升試，是名「退送」。

translations.literal: All presented scholars entering the Bright Hall outer hall who failed to qualify for advancement and replenishment in three examinations, or failed to place in two examinations and still incurred penalties of the three highest grades, had their registers struck and had to retake their home prefecture's annual-advancement examination; this was called "return and dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholars entering the Bright Hall outer hall who failed to qualify for advancement in three examinations, or failed to place in two examinations while incurring penalties of the three highest grades, were struck from the register and sent back to retake their home prefecture's annual-advancement examination. This was called "return and dispatch."

sentences.zh: 即內舍已降舍，而又一試不與，或兩犯上四等罰者，亦如外舍法退送。

translations.literal: If inner-hall students already demoted in hall failed again in one examination, or incurred penalties of the four highest grades twice, they were likewise returned and dispatched under the outer-hall rule.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-hall students already demoted in hall who failed one more examination, or who incurred penalties of the four highest grades twice, were likewise returned and dispatched under the outer-hall rule.

sentences.zh: 太學外舍生巳預考察者，許再經一試，以中否為留遣，餘升降、退送悉如辟雍法。

translations.literal: Imperial College outer-hall students already entered in the merit-review register were permitted one further examination, with pass or fail determining retention or dismissal; all other advancement, demotion, and return-and-dispatch followed Bright Hall regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College outer-hall students already entered in the merit-review register were allowed one further examination, with pass or fail determining whether they stayed or were dismissed. All other advancement, demotion, and return-and-dispatch followed Bright Hall rules.

sentences.zh: 凡有官人不入學而願試貢士者，不以文、武、雜出身，悉許之，惟贓私罪廢人則否。

translations.literal: All appointed officials who did not enter school but wished to test as presented scholars, regardless of civil, military, or miscellaneous credentials, were permitted; only persons disqualified for corruption or private offenses were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed officials who did not enroll in school but wished to test as presented scholars were permitted regardless of civil, military, or miscellaneous credentials. Only persons disqualified for corruption or private offenses were excluded.

sentences.zh: 應試者，隨內外附貢士公試，皆別考，率以七人取一人。

translations.literal: Those sitting the examination attached to inner or outer academies in the presented scholars' public examination, all examined separately, with one selected for every seven persons on average.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates attached to the inner or outer academies sat the presented scholars' public examination separately, with one selected for every seven on average.

sentences.zh: 即預貢者，與辟雍春試貢士通考。

translations.literal: Those pre-presented were examined jointly with Bright Hall spring-examination presented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-presented candidates were examined jointly with Bright Hall spring-examination presented scholars.

sentences.zh: 中選入上等者，升差遣兩等，賜上舍出身；

translations.literal: Those selected in the upper grade were promoted two grades in appointment and granted upper-hall credentials;
translations.idiomatic: Those ranked in the upper grade received promotion two grades in appointment and were granted upper-hall credentials;

sentences.zh: 文行優者，奏聞而殊擢之。

translations.literal: those outstanding in literary accomplishment and conduct were memorialized and specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: those outstanding in literary accomplishment and conduct were memorialized to the throne and specially promoted.

sentences.zh: 中等俟殿試，下等補內舍，不隸學，需再試。

translations.literal: The middle grade awaited the palace examination; the lower grade was placed in the inner hall without enrollment and required re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: The middle grade awaited the palace examination; the lower grade was placed in the inner hall without formal enrollment and had to sit for re-examination.

sentences.zh: 已仕在官而願試者，悉準此制。

translations.literal: Those already in office who wished to test all followed this system.
translations.idiomatic: Those already serving in office who wished to test were all subject to this system.

sentences.zh: 凡在外官同居小功以上親，及其親姊妹女之夫，皆得為隨行親，免試入所任鄰州郡學。

translations.literal: All relatives within mourning-grade xiaogong and above living together with officials serving outside the capital, and the husbands of their sisters and daughters, could serve as accompanying relatives and enter the neighboring prefectural school of the official's post without examination.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives within mourning-grade xiaogong and above living together with officials serving outside the capital, and the husbands of their sisters and daughters, could serve as accompanying relatives and enter the neighboring prefectural school of the official's post without examination.

sentences.zh: 其有官人願學於本州者，亦免試，升補悉如諸生法，混試同考，惟升舍不侵諸生額，自用七人取一。

translations.literal: Officials wishing to study in their home prefecture were also exempt from examination; advancement and replenishment followed ordinary-student regulations, with mixed examinations and joint testing, except that hall advancement did not encroach on ordinary-student quotas and used its own rate of one in seven.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wishing to study in their home prefecture were also exempt from examination. Advancement and replenishment followed ordinary-student rules, with mixed examinations and joint testing, except that hall advancement did not encroach on ordinary-student quotas and used its own one-in-seven selection rate.

sentences.zh: 若中者多，即以溢額名次理為考察。

translations.literal: If many passed, the overflow quota was ranked by order and entered into merit review.
translations.idiomatic: If many passed, the overflow was ranked by order and entered into the merit-review register.

sentences.zh: 若所親移替，願改籍他州學者聽。

translations.literal: If the relative official was transferred or replaced, those wishing to change registration to another prefectural school were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If the relative official was transferred or replaced, those wishing to transfer registration to another prefectural school were permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 太學上、內舍既由辟雍升入，又已罷科舉，則國子監解額無所用，盡均撥諸府、諸州解額，三分之，以為三歲貢額，並令有司均定以聞。

translations.literal: Since Imperial College upper- and inner-hall students now advanced from the Bright Hall and the civil-service examinations had been abolished, Directorate recommendation quotas were no longer needed; they were evenly distributed among metropolitan and prefectural recommendation quotas, divided into thirds as three-year presentation quotas, and officials were ordered to fix the distribution evenly and report.
translations.idiomatic: Since Imperial College upper- and inner-hall students now advanced from the Bright Hall and the civil-service examinations had been abolished, Directorate recommendation quotas were no longer needed. They were evenly distributed among metropolitan and prefectural recommendation quotas, divided into thirds as three-year presentation quotas, and officials were ordered to fix the distribution and report.

sentences.zh: 太學舊制，止分立優、平二等，自今欲令辟雍、太學試上舍中程者，皆參用察考，以差升補。

translations.literal: Under the old Imperial College system only superior and fair grades were distinguished; from now on it was desired that upper-hall candidates passing the standard in Bright Hall and Imperial College examinations all cross-reference conduct assessment for differential advancement and replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Imperial College system only superior and fair grades were distinguished. Henceforth, upper-hall candidates passing the standard in Bright Hall and Imperial College examinations would all cross-reference conduct assessment for differential advancement and replenishment.

sentences.zh: 其考察試格，悉分上、中、下三等。

translations.literal: Merit-review and examination standards were all divided into upper, middle, and lower grades.
translations.idiomatic: Standards for merit review and examination were all divided into upper, middle, and lower tiers.

sentences.zh: 貢士則以本州升貢等第，太學內舍則以校定等第。

translations.literal: For presented scholars, the home prefecture's presentation grade was used; for Imperial College inner-hall students, the school-fixed grade was used.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholars were graded by their home prefecture's presentation rank; Imperial College inner-hall students were graded by the rank fixed by the school.

sentences.zh: 每上舍試考已定，知舉及學官以中試之等參驗於籍，通定升絀高下，兩上為上，一上一中及兩中為中，一上一下及一中下、兩下為下。
