translations.literal: Whenever upper-hall examination grades were fixed, chief examiners and school officials cross-checked examination grades against the register and determined overall advancement and demotion: two upper grades counted as upper; one upper and one middle, or two middles, counted as middle; one upper and one lower, one middle and one lower, or two lowers counted as lower.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever upper-hall examination grades were fixed, chief examiners and school officials cross-checked examination grades against the register to determine overall advancement and demotion: two upper grades ranked as upper; one upper and one middle, or two middles, ranked as middle; one upper and one lower, one middle and one lower, or two lowers ranked as lower.

sentences.zh: 若兩格名次等第適皆齊同，即以試等壓考察之格，餘率以是為差，仍推其法達之諸州。

translations.literal: If the ranks and grades of both standards happened to be entirely identical, examination grade took precedence over merit-review grade; the remainder followed this principle for differentiation, and the method was extended to all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: If the ranks and grades of both standards happened to be entirely identical, examination grade took precedence over merit-review grade. The remainder followed this principle for differentiation, and the method was extended to all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡內外私試，始改用仲月，並試三場，試論日仍添律義。

translations.literal: All inner and outer private examinations were first changed to the middle month of each season, with three sessions in all; on the discourse-examination day exposition of statutes was added.
translations.idiomatic: All inner and outer private examinations were changed to the middle month of each season, with three sessions in all. On the discourse-examination day, exposition of statutes was added.

sentences.zh: 凡考察悉準在學人數，每內舍十人取五，外舍十人取六，自上而下分為三等籍，以俟上舍考定而參用之。

translations.literal: All merit review was based on enrolled numbers: for every ten inner-hall students five were taken, for every ten outer-hall students six; from top to bottom they were divided into three-grade registers to await upper-hall examination determination for cross-reference.
translations.idiomatic: All merit review was based on enrolled numbers: five of every ten inner-hall students and six of every ten outer-hall students were selected, ranked from top to bottom in three-grade registers to await cross-reference when upper-hall examinations were finalized.

sentences.zh: 是歲，貢士至辟雍不如令者，凡三十有八人，皆罷歸，而提學官皆罰金。

translations.literal: That year, presented scholars arriving at the Bright Hall who failed to meet regulations numbered thirty-eight in all; all were dismissed and sent home, and the school intendants were all fined.
translations.idiomatic: That year, thirty-eight presented scholars arriving at the Bright Hall failed to meet regulations. All were dismissed and sent home, and the school intendants were all fined.

sentences.zh: 建州浦城縣學生，隸籍者至千餘人，為一路最，縣丞徐秉哲特遷一官。

translations.literal: Students of Pucheng County in Jian Prefecture on the register numbered more than one thousand, the highest in the circuit; Assistant Magistrate Xu Bingzhe was specially promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: More than one thousand students of Pucheng County in Jian Prefecture were on the register—the highest in the circuit—and Assistant Magistrate Xu Bingzhe was specially promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 初立八行科，詔曰：「學以善風俗，明人倫，而人材所自出也。

translations.literal: When the Eight-Conducts category was first established, an edict said: "Learning is to improve customs, clarify human relations, and is the source from which talent emerges.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight-Conducts category was first established, an edict declared: "Learning improves customs, clarifies human relations, and is the source from which talent emerges.

sentences.zh: 今法制未立，殆無以厲天下。

translations.literal: Now regulations are not yet established, and there is scarcely means to encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet regulations are not yet established, and there is scarcely any means to encourage the realm.

sentences.zh: 成周以六行賓興萬民，否則威之以不孝、不弟之刑。

translations.literal: The completed Zhou used the Six Conducts to guest-elevate the myriad people; otherwise they were awed with punishments for lack of filial piety and fraternal duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou at its height used the Six Conducts to elevate the people; otherwise they enforced punishments for lack of filial piety and fraternal duty.

sentences.zh: 近因稽周法，立八行、八刑，頒之學校，兼行懲勸，庶幾於古。

translations.literal: Recently, in investigating Zhou methods, the Eight Conducts and Eight Punishments were established, promulgated to schools, punishment and encouragement applied together, hoping to approach antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, drawing on Zhou methods, the court established the Eight Conducts and Eight Punishments, issued them to schools, and applied both reward and penalty together in the hope of approximating ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 士有善父母為孝，善兄弟為悌，善內親為睦，善外親為姻，信於朋友為任，仁於州裏為恤，知君臣之義為忠，達義利之分為和。

translations.literal: For scholars: being good to parents is filial piety; being good to brothers is fraternal duty; being good to inner kin is concord; being good to outer kin is affinity; being trustworthy with friends is reliability; being benevolent in the district is compassion; knowing the meaning of ruler and minister is loyalty; comprehending the distinction of righteousness and profit is harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For scholars, filial piety meant treating one's parents well; fraternal duty, one's brothers; concord, close relatives; affinity, more distant kin; reliability, trustworthiness among friends; compassion, kindness toward neighbors; loyalty, understanding the obligations between ruler and subject; and harmony, grasping the difference between righteousness and profit.

sentences.zh: 凡有八行實狀，鄉上之縣，縣延入學，審考無偽，上其名於州。

translations.literal: Whenever there was verified evidence of the Eight Conducts, the township reported upward to the county; the county invited the candidate into school, examined and verified that there was no fraud, and submitted his name to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When a candidate had documented proof of the Eight Conducts, the township reported him to the county, the county invited him into school and verified that the record was genuine, and then forwarded his name to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州第其等，孝、悌、忠、和為上，睦、姻為中，任、恤為下。

translations.literal: The prefecture ranked the grades: filial piety, fraternal duty, loyalty, and harmony were upper; concord and affinity were middle; reliability and compassion were lower.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture ranked candidates by grade: filial piety, fraternal duty, loyalty, and harmony counted as upper; concord and affinity as middle; reliability and compassion as lower.

sentences.zh: 苟備八行，不俟終歲，即奏貢入太學，免試補為上舍。

translations.literal: If one fully possessed the Eight Conducts, without waiting for the year's end, he was immediately memorialized and presented to the Imperial College, exempt from examination and replenished as an upper-hall student.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fully met all Eight Conducts could, without waiting out the year, be memorialized and sent directly to the Imperial College, exempt from examination and admitted straight into the upper hall.

sentences.zh: 司成以下審考不誣，申省釋褐，優命之官；

translations.literal: The Director of Students and those below examined and verified that there was no deception, reported to the province for release from common dress, and favorably appointed them to office;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Students and his subordinates reviewed the record to ensure it was not false, reported to the province for release from student status, and favorably appointed the candidates to office;

sentences.zh: 不能全備者，為州學上等上舍，餘有差。」

translations.literal: Those unable to fully possess all were made upper-grade upper-hall students at the prefectural school; the remainder received differential treatment."
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not fully meet all eight standards were placed in the upper grade of the prefectural school's upper hall, with lesser distinctions for the rest."

sentences.zh: 八刑則反八行而麗於罪，各以其罪名之。

translations.literal: The Eight Punishments then countered the Eight Conducts and were attached to crimes, each named by its crime title.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Punishments were the inverse of the Eight Conducts and were tied to specific offenses, each named after the corresponding crime.

sentences.zh: 縣上其名於州，州稽於學，毋得補弟子員。

translations.literal: The county submitted his name to the prefecture; the prefecture checked with the school, and he was not permitted to be replenished on the student register.
translations.idiomatic: The county reported the offender's name to the prefecture, the prefecture verified the matter with the school, and he was barred from replenishment on the student register.

sentences.zh: 然品目既立，有司必求其跡以應令，遂有牽合瑣細者。

translations.literal: Yet once the categories were established, officials had to seek traces to meet the order, and there were forced matches on trivial details.
translations.idiomatic: But once the categories were fixed, officials felt compelled to find evidence that fit the regulations, and people began forcing trivial acts to match the required labels.

sentences.zh: 自元祐創經明行修科，主德行而略辭藝，間取禮部試黜之士，附寘恩科，當時固已咎其無所甄別。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanyou period created the category of Classic Clarity and Conduct Cultivation, emphasizing virtue and slighting literary skill, occasionally taking candidates failed in the Ministry of Rites examination and placing them in the grace category, it was already criticized at the time for lacking discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: When the Classic Clarity and Conduct Cultivation category was created in the Yuanyou period, it emphasized moral conduct over literary skill and sometimes admitted candidates who had failed the Ministry of Rites examination through the grace category; even then it was criticized for failing to distinguish true merit.

sentences.zh: 及八行科立，則三舍皆不試而補，往往設為形跡，求與名格相應。

translations.literal: When the Eight-Conducts category was established, all three halls were replenished without examination, and people often set up appearances seeking to match the nominal standards.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Eight-Conducts category was established, students in all three halls could advance without examination, and candidates often staged outward signs of virtue simply to fit the formal categories.

sentences.zh: 於是兩科相望幾數十年，乃無一人卓然能自著見者，而八行又有甚敝。

translations.literal: Thus the two categories spanned nearly several decades without a single person outstanding who could distinguish himself, and the Eight Conducts had grave abuses besides.
translations.idiomatic: Across the decades that the two categories ran in parallel, not one candidate stood out as genuinely distinguished, while the Eight-Conducts system itself fell into serious abuse.

sentences.zh: 蓋後世欲追古制，而不知風俗教化之所從出，其難固如此夫。

translations.literal: For later ages seeking to follow ancient institutions yet not knowing whence custom and moral instruction arise, the difficulty is indeed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages sought to revive ancient institutions without understanding where custom and moral instruction truly come from; the difficulty was bound to be exactly such as this.

sentences.zh: 開封始建府學，立貢士額凡五十，而士子不及三百，盡額而取，則涉太優，欲稍裁之。

translations.literal: When Kaifeng first established its prefectural school, the quota for presented scholars was set at fifty, but scholars numbered fewer than three hundred; taking the full quota would be excessively generous, and officials wished to trim it slightly.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaifeng first established its prefectural school, it set a presentation quota of fifty scholars, though fewer than three hundred candidates were enrolled. Filling the quota entirely seemed too generous, and officials wanted to reduce it somewhat.

sentences.zh: 詔：「王畿立學，若不優誘使進，何以首善？

translations.literal: An edict said: "In establishing schools in the metropolitan region, if they are not favorably induced to advance, how can they lead in goodness?
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "If schools in the capital region are not generously encouraged to advance their students, how can the realm look to them as the model of excellence?

sentences.zh: 其常解五十勿闕。」

translations.literal: The regular quota of fifty should not be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: The standing quota of fifty must not be cut."

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，詔願兼他經者，量立升進之法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, an edict ordered that for those wishing to combine other classics, promotion methods should be established by measure.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 1, an edict directed that measured rules for advancement be established for students who wished to study additional classics alongside their primary one.

sentences.zh: 大抵用本經決去取，而兼經所中等第特為升貢。

translations.literal: Generally the primary classic decided selection and rejection, while a middle grade in the secondary classic was specially used for elevated presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In general, selection rested on the primary classic, but a middle grade in a secondary classic could qualify a candidate for special elevated presentation.

sentences.zh: 每歲附公試院而別異其號，每十五人取一人，分上、中、下等，別榜示之，唱名日，甄別奏聞，與升甲，皆優於專經者。

translations.literal: Each year they were attached to the public examination hall under a separate designation; one person was taken from every fifteen, divided into upper, middle, and lower grades and shown on a separate list; on announcement day they were distinguished, reported to the throne, and given rank elevation—all superior to specialists in a single classic.
translations.idiomatic: Each year these candidates were examined in the public examination hall under a separate designation, with one selected from every fifteen and ranked upper, middle, or lower on a separate list. On announcement day their results were reported to the throne and they received rank elevation, all on terms more favorable than those for single-classic specialists.

sentences.zh: 異時內外學官闕，皆得在選。

translations.literal: When vacancies arose among inner and outer school officials, all were eligible for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever posts opened among school officials in the capital and in the provinces, these candidates were all eligible for appointment.

sentences.zh: 縣學生三不赴歲升試及三赴歲升試而不能升州學者，皆除其籍。

translations.literal: County students who three times failed to attend the annual promotion examination, or who three times attended the annual promotion examination yet could not advance to the prefectural school, were all removed from the register.
translations.idiomatic: County students who missed the annual promotion examination three times, or who took it three times without advancing to the prefectural school, were all struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 諸路賓興會試辟雍，獨常州中選者多，州守若教授俱遷一官。

translations.literal: At the circuit preparatory assemblies and Bright Hall examinations, Changzhou alone had many selected; both the prefect and the instructor were each promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the circuit preparatory assemblies and Bright Hall examinations, Changzhou alone produced an unusually large number of successful candidates, and both the prefect and the instructor were promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，小學生近一千人，分十齋以處之，自八歲至十二歲，率以誦經書字多少差次補內舍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, elementary students numbered nearly one thousand; they were divided into ten halls for accommodation. From ages eight to twelve, they were generally ranked by how many characters of scripture they could recite and replenished into the inner hall accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 4, nearly one thousand elementary students were housed in ten halls. Boys aged eight to twelve were generally ranked by how much scripture they could recite and admitted to the inner hall accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若能文，從博士試本經、小經義各一道，稍通補內舍，優補上舍。

translations.literal: If able in writing, they were tested by the erudite on one question each of primary-classic exegesis and minor-classic exegesis; slight competence replenished them into the inner hall, and excellence replenished them into the upper hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those who showed literary ability were tested by the erudite on one question each from the primary and minor classics; modest competence gained admission to the inner hall, and strong performance to the upper hall.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「學校教養額少，則野有遺士，應諸路學校及百人以上者，三分增一。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: "If school nurturing quotas are too small, neglected scholars remain in the countryside; circuits whose schools number one hundred persons or more should increase enrollment by one third."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "When school enrollment quotas are too small, talented men are left untrained in the countryside. Every circuit whose schools already enrolled one hundred students or more should increase those quotas by one third."

sentences.zh: 七年，試高麗進士權適等四人，皆賜上舍及第，遣歸其國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, four Goryeo jinshi including Quan Shi were examined; all were granted upper-hall completion and sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, four Goryeo degree candidates including Quan Shi were examined, all were granted upper-hall completion, and were sent home to their country.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣留意學校，因事究敝，有司考閱防閑益密。

translations.literal: At the time chief ministers paid attention to schools; as incidents arose they investigated abuses, and officials' review and preventive oversight grew increasingly strict.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers were closely attentive to the schools; when problems arose they investigated abuses, and official review and preventive oversight grew steadily tighter.

sentences.zh: 先是，禮部上《雜修禦試貢士敕令格式》，又取舊制凡關學政者，分敕、令、格、式，成書以上。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Ministry of Rites submitted the 《Miscellaneous Revised Imperial Examination Presented Scholar Edicts, Orders, Standards, and Formats》; it also gathered old regulations concerning school administration, divided them into edicts, orders, standards, and formats, compiled them into a book, and submitted it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Ministry of Rites had submitted the 《Miscellaneous Revised Imperial Examination Presented Scholar Edicts, Orders, Standards, and Formats》, and had also collected every old regulation bearing on school administration, arranged them under edicts, orders, standards, and formats, compiled them into a book, and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 用給事中毛友言，初試補入縣學生，並簾試以別偽冒。

translations.literal: Following the proposal of Reminder of the Secretariat Mao You, initial examinations for replenishment as county students were all conducted as curtain examinations to distinguish fraud and impersonation.
translations.idiomatic: Following a proposal by Reminder of the Secretariat Mao You, all initial examinations for admission as county students were conducted behind curtained booths to expose fraud and impersonation.

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇尚老氏之學，知兗州王純乞於《御注道德經》注中出論題，範致虛亦乞用《聖濟經》出題。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong venerated the learning of Laozi; Wang Chun, prefect of Yanzhou, requested that essay topics be drawn from the commentary to the 《Imperially Annotated Dao De Jing》, and Fan Zhixu also requested that the 《Shengji Jing》 be used for examination topics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong favored Laozi's teachings. Wang Chun, prefect of Yanzhou, asked that essay topics be drawn from the commentary to the 《Imperially Annotated Dao De Jing》, and Fan Zhixu asked that the 《Shengji Jing》 be used as an examination source as well.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，帝親取貢士卷考定，能深通《內經》者，升之以為第一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, the Emperor personally took presented scholars' examination papers to examine and fix the grades; those who deeply mastered the 《Inner Classic》 were elevated and made first.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1, the Emperor personally reviewed the examination papers of presented scholars and ranked them himself, elevating to first place those who showed deep mastery of the 《Inner Classic》.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔：「罷天下州縣學三舍法，惟太學用之課試。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said: "Abolish the three-hall method in schools throughout the realm's prefectures and counties; only the Imperial College shall use it for course examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict ordered: "Abolish the three-hall system in prefectural and county schools throughout the empire. Only the Imperial College shall retain it for graded examinations.

sentences.zh: 開封府及諸路，並以科舉取士。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture and all circuits alike shall select scholars through the civil-service examination.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture and all circuits alike were to select scholars through the civil-service examination.

sentences.zh: 太學官吏及州縣嘗置學官，凡元豐舊制所有者皆如故，其辟雍官屬及宗學並諸路提舉學事官屬並罷，內外學悉遵元豐成憲。」

translations.literal: Imperial College officials and prefectural and county school officials formerly established—all those under the old Yuanfeng system were restored as before; the Bright Hall staff, the imperial-clan school, and the circuit school-intendant staffs were all abolished, and inner and outer schools all followed the Yuanfeng statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Imperial College and of prefectural and county schools were restored wherever the Yuanfeng system had once provided for them. The Bright Hall staff, the imperial-clan school, and circuit school intendants were all abolished, and inner and outer schools were ordered to follow the Yuanfeng statutes."

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：「政和中嘗命學校分治黃、老、莊、列之書，實失專經之旨，其《內經》等書並罷治。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict said: "In the Zhenghe period schools were once ordered to teach separately the books of Huang-Lao, Zhuangzi, and Liezi; this truly lost the aim of specializing in the classics. The 《Inner Classic》 and such books are all abolished from instruction."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict declared: "During the Zhenghe period schools were once ordered to teach separately the texts of Huang-Lao, Zhuangzi, and Liezi, which in truth departed from the purpose of classical specialization. Instruction in the 《Inner Classic》 and similar works is hereby abolished."

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來，士子各徇其黨，習經義則詆元祐之非，尚詞賦則誚新經之失，互相排斥，群論紛紛。

translations.literal: Since Chongning, scholars each followed their faction: those studying classic exegesis denounced the errors of the Yuanyou period; those honoring regulated verse and rhapsody mocked the faults of the new classics; they mutually excluded one another, and public debate grew clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chongning period, scholars had divided along factional lines: those trained in classic exegesis denounced the Yuanyou reforms, while those devoted to regulated verse and rhapsody mocked the new classics. They rejected one another, and public debate grew increasingly bitter.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，臣僚言：「科舉取士，要當質以史學，詢以時政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong acceded, officials said: "In selecting scholars through the civil-service examination, one must test them substantively in historical learning and inquire into current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong came to the throne, officials argued: "In selecting scholars by examination, candidates should be tested rigorously in historical learning and questioned closely on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 今之策問，虛無不根，古今治亂，悉所不曉。

translations.literal: Today's policy questions are empty and rootless; order and disorder in ancient and modern times they do not understand at all.
translations.idiomatic: Today's policy questions are empty and groundless, and candidates show no understanding at all of order and disorder in past or present.

sentences.zh: 詩賦設科，所得名臣，不可勝紀，專試經義亦已五紀。

translations.literal: When poetry and rhapsody formed a category, the eminent ministers obtained are too many to count; exclusive examination in classic exegesis has already lasted five decades.
translations.idiomatic: The poetry and rhapsody examinations produced eminent ministers beyond number, while examination in classic exegesis alone has already lasted fifty years.

sentences.zh: 救之之術，莫若遵用祖宗成憲。

translations.literal: The method of remedy is none better than following and using the established statutes of the ancestral founders.
translations.idiomatic: The best remedy is to return to the established statutes of the founding emperors.

sentences.zh: 王安石解經，有不背聖人旨意，亦許采用。

translations.literal: In Wang Anshi's exegesis of the classics, passages that do not depart from the intent of the sages should also be permitted for adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Where Wang Anshi's exegeses do not depart from the intent of the sages, they too should be permitted for use.

sentences.zh: 至於老、莊之書及《字說》，並應禁止。」

translations.literal: As for the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi and the 《Character Explanations》, all should be prohibited."
translations.idiomatic: As for the texts of Laozi and Zhuangzi and the 《Character Explanations》, all should be banned from the curriculum."

sentences.zh: 詔禮部詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Ministry of Rites to consider the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫兼祭酒楊時言：「王安石著為邪說，以塗學者耳目，使蔡京之徒，得以輕費妄用，極侈靡以奉上，幾危社稷。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Policy Grandee and concurrent Libationer Yang Shi said: "Wang Anshi wrote heterodox doctrines to smear the eyes and ears of scholars, enabling men such as Cai Jing to spend lightly and use recklessly, pursuing extreme extravagance to please the throne and nearly endangering the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Policy Grandee and concurrent Libationer Yang Shi argued: "Wang Anshi composed heterodox doctrines that misled scholars, enabling men such as Cai Jing to spend recklessly, pursue extreme extravagance to please the throne, and nearly bring the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 乞奪安石配饗，使邪說不能為學者惑。」

translations.literal: I beg that Anshi be stripped of his place in the paired sacrifice, so that heterodox doctrines cannot delude scholars."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Wang Anshi be removed from the paired sacrifice in the temple, so that his heterodox doctrines can no longer mislead scholars."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞陳過庭言：「《五經》義微，諸家異見，以所是者為正，所否者為邪，此一偏之大失也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Chen Guoting said: "The meaning of the 《Five Classics》 is subtle, and schools hold differing views; to treat what one approves as orthodox and what one rejects as heterodox is a great error of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Chen Guoting replied: "The meaning of the 《Five Classics》 is subtle, and schools of interpretation differ. To call what one favors orthodox and what one rejects heterodox is a grave error of partisan judgment.

sentences.zh: 頃者指蘇軾為邪學，而加禁甚切；

translations.literal: Not long ago Su Shi was labeled heterodox learning and the prohibition was very strict;
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Su Shi was denounced as a purveyor of heterodox learning and the ban against him was very strict;

sentences.zh: 今已弛其禁，許采其長，實為通論。

translations.literal: now the prohibition has already been relaxed and his strengths are permitted for adoption—this is truly a comprehensive view.
translations.idiomatic: now that ban has been relaxed and his strengths may be adopted—an approach that is truly balanced.

sentences.zh: 而祭酒楊時矯枉太過，復詆王氏以為邪說，此又非也。」

translations.literal: Yet Libationer Yang Shi overcorrects too far, again denouncing the Wang school as heterodox doctrine—this too is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Libationer Yang Shi overcorrects in the opposite direction by denouncing the Wang school anew as heterodox doctrine—and that too is wrong."

sentences.zh: 諸生習用王學，聞時之言，群起而詆詈之，時引避不出，齋生始散。

translations.literal: The students, accustomed to the Wang school, upon hearing Yang Shi's words rose together to revile him; Yang withdrew and would not come out, and only then did the hall students disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Students trained in the Wang school, hearing Yang Shi's remarks, rose together to revile him. Yang withdrew and refused to appear until the hall students finally dispersed.

sentences.zh: 詔罷時祭酒。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Yang Shi from the libationership.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Yang Shi from the post of libationer.

sentences.zh: 而諫議大夫馮澥、崔鶠等復更相辨論，會國事危，而貢舉不及行矣。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Policy Grandees Feng Xi, Cui Yan, and others again debated one another in turn; as state affairs grew perilous, the presentation and selection examinations could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Policy Grandees Feng Xi, Cui Yan, and others then resumed debating one another, but as the state fell into crisis the presentation and selection examinations were never held.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，即行在置國子監，立博士二員，以隨幸之士三十六人為監生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, the Directorate of Education was immediately established at the mobile court, with two erudites appointed and thirty-six scholars who had accompanied the imperial flight made Directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, the court immediately established the Directorate of Education at the mobile capital, appointed two erudites, and enrolled thirty-six scholars who had accompanied the imperial flight as Directorate students.

sentences.zh: 紹興八年，葉綝上書請建學，而廷臣皆以兵興饋運為辭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shaoxing, Ye Lin memorialized requesting the establishment of a school, but court officials all used the rising of war and costly transport as their excuse.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 8, Ye Lin submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of a school, but court officials all pleaded the ongoing war and the high cost of transport.

sentences.zh: 十三年，兵事稍寧，始建太學，置祭酒、司業各一員，博士三員，正、錄各一員，養士七百人：上舍生三十員，內舍生百員，外舍生五百七十員。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, as military affairs grew somewhat calm, the Imperial College was first established, with one libationer, one vice director, three erudites, and one registrar and one recorder each; seven hundred scholars were nurtured: thirty upper-hall students, one hundred inner-hall students, and five hundred seventy outer-hall students.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, once military affairs had eased somewhat, the Imperial College was finally established with one libationer, one vice director, three erudites, and one registrar and one recorder. Enrollment was set at seven hundred students: thirty in the upper hall, one hundred in the inner hall, and five hundred seventy in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 凡諸道住本州學滿一年，三試中選，不犯第三等以上罰，或不住學而曾兩預釋奠及齒於鄉飲酒者，聽充弟子員。

translations.literal: Generally, those in each circuit who resided at their home prefectural school for a full year, were selected in three examinations, incurred no punishment of third grade or above, or who though not residing at school had twice participated in the libation sacrifice and taken part in the district drinking ceremony, were permitted to serve as student members.
translations.idiomatic: In general, candidates from each circuit who had studied at their home prefectural school for a full year, passed three examinations, and incurred no punishment of third grade or above—or who, though not enrolled at school, had twice attended the libation sacrifice and the district drinking ceremony—were permitted to serve as student members.

sentences.zh: 每歲春秋兩試之，旋命一歲一補，於是多士雲集，至分場試之。

translations.literal: Each year they were examined in spring and autumn; soon an order came for replenishment once a year, and many scholars gathered like clouds, until examinations had to be held in separate venues.
translations.idiomatic: They were examined each spring and autumn, and replenishment was soon fixed at once a year. Scholars gathered in such numbers that examinations had to be held in separate venues.

sentences.zh: 俄又詔三年一試，增至千員，中選者皆給綾紙讚詞以寵之。

translations.literal: Soon another edict ordered examinations once every three years, increased enrollment to one thousand, and all who were selected were given silk paper with laudatory words to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict changed the cycle to one examination every three years, raised enrollment to one thousand, and granted successful candidates silk certificates bearing laudatory inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 每科場四取其一。

translations.literal: For each examination session one person was taken from every four.
translations.idiomatic: At each examination one candidate was selected from every four.

sentences.zh: 自外舍有月校，而公試入等曰內舍；

translations.literal: From the outer hall there were monthly reviews, and entering a grade in the public examination was called the inner hall;
translations.idiomatic: Students in the outer hall underwent monthly reviews, and passing the public examination gained them admission to the inner hall;

sentences.zh: 自內舍有月校，而舍試入等曰上舍；

translations.literal: from the inner hall there were monthly reviews, and entering a grade in the hall examination was called the upper hall;
translations.idiomatic: students in the inner hall likewise had monthly reviews, and passing the hall examination gained them admission to the upper hall;

sentences.zh: 凡升上舍者，皆直赴廷對。

translations.literal: all who advanced to the upper hall went directly to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: and all who advanced to the upper hall proceeded directly to a court audience.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，立定制：春季放補，遇省試年改用孟夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year a fixed regulation was established: replenishment was released in spring, but in years of the provincial examination it was changed to early summer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year a fixed rule was established: replenishment was held in spring, but in years when the provincial examination was held it was moved to early summer.

sentences.zh: 舊，太學遇覃恩無免解法，孝宗始創行之。

translations.literal: Formerly, when the Imperial College encountered a broad grace there was no exemption from the qualifying examination; Emperor Xiaozong first created and implemented this practice.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Imperial College had no exemption from the qualifying examination even during broad grace amnesties; Emperor Xiaozong was the first to institute such exemptions.

sentences.zh: 在朝清要官，許牒期親子弟作待補國子，別號考校。

translations.literal: Important officials at court were permitted to memorialize close relatives' sons and nephews as awaiting-replenishment Directorate students under a separate designation for examination and review.
translations.idiomatic: Important officials at court were permitted to nominate close relatives' sons and nephews as awaiting-replenishment Directorate students, who were examined under a separate designation.

sentences.zh: 如太學生遇有期親任清要官，更為國子生，不預校定、升補及差職事，惟得赴公、私試，科舉則混試焉。

translations.literal: If an Imperial College student had a close relative serving as an important official, he was changed to a Directorate student, did not participate in school review, advancement, replenishment, or assignment of duties, but was only permitted to attend public and private examinations; in the civil-service examination he was mixed into the general examination.
translations.idiomatic: If an Imperial College student had a close relative serving as an important official, he was transferred to Directorate status, exempt from school review, advancement, replenishment, and official assignments, but still permitted to take public and private examinations; in the civil-service examination he competed in the general pool.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，命諸生暇日習射，以鬥力為等差，比類公、私試，別理分數。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi period, students were ordered on free days to practice archery, with grades differentiated by contest of strength; this was compared with public and private examinations and scored separately.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi period, students were ordered to practice archery on free days, ranked by strength in competition; the results were scored separately, on the model of public and private examinations.

sentences.zh: 自中興以來，四方之士，有本貫在學公據，皆得就補。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, scholars from all directions who had official certification of native place and school enrollment were all permitted to seek replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, scholars from all quarters who held official certification of native place and school enrollment were all permitted to seek admission.

sentences.zh: 帝始加限節，命諸路州軍以解試終場人數為準，其薦貢不盡者，令百取六人赴太學，謂之「待補生」；

translations.literal: The Emperor first imposed limits, ordering each circuit's prefectures and garrisons to take the number finishing the qualifying examination as the standard; where recommended presentations did not fill the quota, six persons were taken from every hundred to go to the Imperial College, called "awaiting-replenishment students";
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then imposed restrictions, ordering each circuit's prefectures and garrisons to base quotas on the number finishing the qualifying examination. Where recommended presentations fell short, six candidates were taken from every hundred to enter the Imperial College as "awaiting-replenishment students";

sentences.zh: 其住本學及遊學之類，一切禁止。

translations.literal: residence at one's home school and traveling study and the like were all prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: admission based on residence at one's home school or on traveling study was entirely prohibited.

sentences.zh: 元豐舊制，內舍生校定，分優、平二等。

translations.literal: Under the old Yuanfeng system, inner-hall students in school review were divided into superior and fair grades.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Yuanfeng system, inner-hall students were ranked in school review as either superior or fair.

sentences.zh: 優等再赴舍試，又入優，則謂之兩優釋褐，中選者即命以京秩，除學官。

translations.literal: Those of superior grade who again took the hall examination and again entered superior were called "double-superior release from common dress"; those selected were immediately appointed to capital rank and assigned as school officials.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-hall students ranked superior who then took the hall examination and again placed superior were said to have achieved "double-superior release from student status"; successful candidates were immediately appointed to capital rank and assigned as school officials.

sentences.zh: 至是，始令先注職官，代還，注職事官，恩例視進士第二人。

translations.literal: At this point it was first ordered that they first be registered for an official post, and after replacement and return be registered for a duty post; the grace precedent was treated like the second-place jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the rule was changed so that they were first registered for an official post, and after completing a tour of replacement duty were registered for a substantive appointment, with privileges equivalent to those of the second-place jinshi.

sentences.zh: 舊校定歲額五六分為優選者，增為十分矣。

translations.literal: Formerly five or six tenths of the annual school-review quota were chosen as superior; this was increased to ten tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly five or six tenths of the annual school-review quota had been ranked superior; that proportion was now raised to ten tenths.

sentences.zh: 光宗初，公試始令附省場別院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Guangzong's reign, the public examination was first ordered attached to a separate courtyard of the provincial examination grounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Guangzong's reign, the public examination was first held in a separate courtyard attached to the provincial examination grounds.

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年，禮部侍郎倪思請復混補法，命兩省、台諫雜議可否。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxi, Vice Minister of Rites Ni Si requested restoration of the mixed-replenishment method, and the two departments, the Censorate, and remonstrance officials were ordered to debate its feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 3, Vice Minister of Rites Ni Si asked that the mixed-replenishment method be restored, and officials of the two departments, the Censorate, and the remonstrance bureaus were ordered to debate the proposal.

sentences.zh: 於是吏部尚書趙汝愚等合奏曰：「國家恢儒右文，京師、郡縣皆有學，慶曆以後，文物彬彬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Personnel Zhao Ruyu and others jointly memorialized: "The state broadly embraces Confucian learning and honors literature; the capital and the prefectures and counties all have schools, and after the Qingli period culture flourished richly.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhao Ruyu and others then jointly memorialized: "The state has broadly embraced Confucian learning and honored literature; schools exist in the capital and in every prefecture and county, and since the Qingli period culture has flourished richly.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，建太學於行都，行貢舉於諸郡，然奔競之風勝，而忠信之俗微。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, the Imperial College has been established at the mobile capital and presentation and selection carried out in the various prefectures, yet the wind of frantic competition prevails while the custom of loyalty and trust grows faint.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration the Imperial College has been established at the mobile capital and presentation and selection carried out in the prefectures, yet frantic competition has prevailed while loyalty and trust have faded.

sentences.zh: 亦惟榮辱升沉，不由學校；

translations.literal: It is also that honor and disgrace, advancement and decline, do not come through the schools;
translations.idiomatic: This is because honor, disgrace, advancement, and decline no longer depend on the schools;

sentences.zh: 德行道藝，取決糊名；

translations.literal: virtue, conduct, and accomplishment are decided by sealed-name examination;
translations.idiomatic: virtue, conduct, and accomplishment are decided by sealed-name examinations;

sentences.zh: 工雕篆之文，無進修之志；

translations.literal: they craft ornate compositions yet lack the will to cultivate themselves;
translations.idiomatic: students polish ornate compositions yet lack any real will to cultivate themselves;

sentences.zh: 視庠序如傳舍，目師儒如路人；

translations.literal: they regard the schools as relay inns and look on teachers as passersby;
translations.idiomatic: they treat the schools like relay inns and their teachers like strangers on the road;

sentences.zh: 季考月書，盡成文具。

translations.literal: seasonal examinations and monthly reports all become empty forms.
translations.idiomatic: seasonal examinations and monthly reports have all become empty formalities.

sentences.zh: 今請重教官之選，假守貳之權；

translations.literal: Now we request emphasizing selection of teaching officials and lending the authority of prefects and vice prefects;
translations.idiomatic: We now ask that greater care be taken in selecting teaching officials and that prefects and vice prefects be given greater authority;

sentences.zh: 仿舍法以育材，因大比以取士；

translations.literal: modeling the hall method to nurture talent and relying on the great comparison to select scholars;
translations.idiomatic: that the hall system be used to nurture talent and the great comparison to select scholars;

sentences.zh: 考終場之數，定所貢之員；

translations.literal: examining the number finishing the final session and fixing the quota to be presented;
translations.idiomatic: that quotas for presentation be fixed according to the number finishing the final examination session;

sentences.zh: 期以次年，試於太學。

translations.literal: setting the following year as the term for examination at the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: and that the following year they be examined at the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 其諸州教養、課試、升貢之法，下有司條上。」

translations.literal: As for methods of nurturing, course examination, and elevated presentation in the various prefectures, lower officials should set them forth in articles and submit them upward."
translations.idiomatic: Detailed rules for nurturing students, course examinations, and elevated presentation in the prefectures should be drafted by the relevant offices and submitted for approval."

sentences.zh: 思議遂寢。

translations.literal: Ni Si's proposal was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Si's proposal was thereupon set aside.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔國子監試中、上等小學生，比類諸州待補中選之額，放補一次。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that elementary students who passed the Directorate examination at middle or upper grade, compared with the quota for awaiting-replenishment selection in the various prefectures, receive one release of replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that elementary students who passed the Directorate examination at middle or upper grade be granted one round of replenishment, on the model of the awaiting-replenishment quota used in the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寧宗慶元、嘉定中，始兩行混補。

translations.literal: In the Qingyuan and Jiading periods of Emperor Ningzong, mixed replenishment was first carried out in both lines.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ningzong's Qingyuan and Jiading reign periods, mixed replenishment was first instituted in both channels.

sentences.zh: 於是增外舍生為千四百員，內舍校定，不係上舍試年分，以八分為優等。

translations.literal: Thereupon outer-hall students were increased to one thousand four hundred; inner-hall school review, not tied to upper-hall examination years, took eight tenths as the superior grade.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-hall enrollment was raised to fourteen hundred students. Inner-hall school review, no longer tied to upper-hall examination years, set the superior grade at eight tenths.

sentences.zh: 又以國子生員多偽濫，命行在職事官期親、厘務官子孫乃得試補。

translations.literal: Also, because many Directorate students were fraudulent and excessive, it was ordered that only close relatives of duty officials at the mobile court and descendants of revenue officials might seek examination replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because many Directorate students were fraudulently enrolled, the court ruled that only close relatives of duty officials at the mobile capital and descendants of revenue officials might seek examination replenishment.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年，詔自今待補百人取三人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, an edict ordered that from now on three persons be taken from every hundred awaiting replenishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 14, an edict fixed the awaiting-replenishment quota at three candidates from every hundred.

sentences.zh: 舊法，自外舍升內舍，雖有校試，必公試合格，乃許升補。

translations.literal: Under the old method, in advancing from the outer hall to the inner hall, although there was a school examination, one had to pass the public examination before advancement and replenishment were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, advancement from the outer hall to the inner hall required passing the school examination, but replenishment was permitted only after passing the public examination as well.

sentences.zh: 蓋私試皆學官自考，而公試則降敕差官。

translations.literal: For private examinations were all self-examined by school officials, while public examinations had officials dispatched by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Private examinations were conducted by school officials themselves, whereas public examinations were supervised by officials dispatched by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 至是，歲終許取外舍生校最優者一人升內舍。

translations.literal: At this point, at year's end one outer-hall student ranked foremost in school review was permitted to advance to the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the rule was changed so that at year's end the top-ranked outer-hall student in school review alone could advance to the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 理宗復百取六人之制。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong restored the system of taking six persons from every hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong restored the quota of six candidates from every hundred.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年，以待補生自外方來參齋者，間有鬻帖偽冒之弊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding, among awaiting-replenishment students coming from outside regions to attend hall sessions, there were occasionally abuses of selling credentials and fraudulent impersonation.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding 2, among awaiting-replenishment students arriving from the provinces to attend hall sessions, there were occasional cases of selling credentials and fraudulent impersonation.

sentences.zh: 遂命中選之人，召升朝保官二員批書印紙，仍命州郡守倅結罪保明，比照字跡無偽，方許簾引注籍；

translations.literal: Thereupon, among those selected in the examination, two court-attending guarantor officials were summoned to endorse the sealed credentials; the prefects and vice prefects of the prefectures and commanderies were also ordered to bond themselves under penalty and certify, and only after comparing handwriting and finding no forgery were curtain-led registration and enrollment permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed the examination were then required to have two court-attending guarantor officials endorse their sealed credentials. Prefects and vice prefects were ordered to certify the candidates under bond of personal liability; only after handwriting was compared and forgery ruled out were candidates led in under the curtain and entered on the register.

sentences.zh: 犯者治罪，罰及保官。

translations.literal: Offenders were punished, and punishment extended to the guarantor officials.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were prosecuted, and their guarantor officials were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 五年，以省試下第及待補生之群試於有司者，有請托賄求之弊，學官考文，有親故交通之私，命今後兩學補試，並從廟堂臨時選差，即令入院；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because those who had failed the provincial examination and awaiting-replenishment students taking group examinations before the authorities had abuses of solicitation and bribery, and because school officials grading papers had private dealings with kin and associates, it was ordered that from now on replenishment examinations at both schools should all be temporarily selected and dispatched by the court, and candidates immediately admitted to the halls;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, provincial examination failures and awaiting-replenishment students sitting group exams before local authorities were found to trade on connections and bribes, while school officials grading papers favored kin and friends. The court therefore ruled that replenishment exams at both schools would hereafter be supervised by officials temporarily dispatched from the capital, with successful candidates admitted to the halls at once.

sentences.zh: 凡用度，則用國子監供給學官事例。

translations.literal: For all expenses, the precedent for supplying school officials at the Directorate of Education was used.
translations.idiomatic: All expenses were covered under the Directorate of Education’s established provisions for supplying school officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，監察御史何處久又言：「宜遵舊制，以武學、宗學補試，並就兩學於大院排日引試，有親嫌人依避房法。

translations.literal: Before long, Investigating Censor He Chujiu again said: "It is fitting to follow the old system, with replenishment examinations for the Military School and the Imperial Clan School both conducted at the two schools in the great hall on scheduled days; where there were kin conflicts, the chamber-avoidance law should apply.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Investigating Censor He Chujiu urged: "Replenishment exams for the Military School and Imperial Clan School should be held on fixed dates in the great hall of the two schools, with the chamber-avoidance law applied wherever kinship conflicts arose.

sentences.zh: 且士子試卷頗多，考官頗少，期日既迫，費用不敷。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the candidates’ examination papers were quite numerous while the examiners were quite few; the deadline was pressing and expenses insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that examination papers far outnumbered the available examiners, deadlines were tight, and funds fell short."

sentences.zh: 乃增給用度，仍添差考官五員。

translations.literal: Funds were then increased, and five additional examiners were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The court increased the budget and added five examiners.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，復命分路取放補試員數，以免遠方士子道路往來之費及都城壅並之患。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou, an order was again issued to distribute replenishment quotas by circuit, so as to spare distant candidates the cost of travel and relieve congestion in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyou 1, replenishment quotas were again distributed by circuit, sparing distant candidates travel costs and easing overcrowding in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，復試於京師。

translations.literal: In the third year, examinations were again held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the exams were moved back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 度宗咸淳二年正月，幸太學，謁先聖，禮成，推恩三學：前廊與免省試，內舍、上舍及已免省試者與升甲；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xianchun under Emperor Duzong, the emperor visited the Imperial College, paid homage to the Sage, and when the rites were complete extended grace to the three schools: the front corridor was granted exemption from the provincial examination; inner-hall, upper-hall, and those already exempt from the provincial examination received rank promotion;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xianchun 2, Emperor Duzong visited the Imperial College and performed rites before the Sage. When the ceremony ended, he extended grace to the three schools: outer-hall students were exempted from the provincial examination; inner-hall and upper-hall students, and those already exempt, received rank promotion.

sentences.zh: 起居學生與泛免一次，內該曾經兩幸人與補上州文學，如願在學者聽。

translations.literal: Attendance students received one general exemption; among them, those who had twice attended imperial visits were granted appointment as upper-prefecture literary officers, and those wishing to remain in school were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Attendance students received one general exemption; those who had twice attended imperial visits were appointed literary officers of upper prefectures, while those who wished to remain enrolled were allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 其在籍諸生，地遠不及趁赴起居者，三學申請乞並行泛免一次，命特從之。

translations.literal: Among enrolled students who lived far away and could not arrive in time for attendance, the three schools petitioned that they too receive one general exemption; the order specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Enrolled students living too far away to attend in person petitioned through the three schools for the same general exemption, and the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 凡諸生升舍在幸學之前者，方許陳乞恩例。

translations.literal: Only students who had advanced in hall rank before the imperial visit to the school were permitted to petition for grace precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Only students who had already advanced in hall rank before the imperial visit were eligible to petition for grace benefits.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，以壽和聖福皇太后兩上尊號，推恩三學，在齋生員並特與免解赴省一次。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, because the Empress Dowager of Longevity, Sacred Blessing, received two honorific titles, grace was extended to the three schools, and all students in residence were specially granted one exemption from qualifying for the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, when the Empress Dowager of Longevity and Sacred Blessing received two honorific titles, grace was extended to the three schools: every student in residence received a special exemption from the provincial qualifying examination.

sentences.zh: 九年，外舍生晏泰亨以七分三氂乞理為第三優，朝命不許，遂申嚴學法，今後及八分者方許歲校三名，如八分者止有一人，而援次優、三優之例者，亦須止少三、二氂，方可陳乞特放，庶不盡廢學法，當亦不過一人而止。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, outer-hall student Yan Taiheng, scoring seven tenths and three li, petitioned to be ranked third superior; the court order did not permit it, and school regulations were thereupon tightened: hereafter only those reaching eight tenths were permitted the three annual school-review top ranks; if only one person reached eight tenths yet invoked the precedents for second or third superior, he still had to fall short by at least two or three li before he could petition for special advancement, so that school law would not be wholly abandoned yet would extend to no more than one person.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, outer-hall student Yan Taiheng, with a score of seven tenths and three li, petitioned to be ranked third superior; the court refused. School regulations were tightened: only scores of eight tenths or higher qualified for the three top annual school-review ranks. If only one student reached eight tenths yet claimed second- or third-superior precedents, he still had to fall short by at least two or three li before seeking special advancement—so that school law would not be wholly discarded yet would rarely benefit more than one student.

sentences.zh: 律學。

translations.literal: Law School.
translations.idiomatic: The Law School.

sentences.zh: 國初置博士，掌授法律。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty a erudite was established to teach law.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty’s founding, an erudite was appointed to teach law.

sentences.zh: 熙寧六年，始即國子監設學，置教授四員。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining, a school was first established within the Directorate of Education, with four instructors appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 6, a Law School was established within the Directorate of Education, with four instructors appointed.

sentences.zh: 凡命官、舉人皆得入學，各處一齋。

translations.literal: Both appointed officials and presented scholars could enter the school, each occupying one hall.
translations.idiomatic: Both appointed officials and presented scholars were eligible to enroll, each assigned to a separate hall.

sentences.zh: 舉人須得命官二人保任，先入學聽讀而後試補。

translations.literal: Presented scholars had to obtain guarantee from two appointed officials, enter the school to listen and read, and only then take the replenishment examination.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholars required sponsorship by two appointed officials; they entered as auditors and could sit for replenishment only afterward.

sentences.zh: 習斷按，則試按一道，每道敘列刑名五事或七事；

translations.literal: Those studying case adjudication were examined on one case, each case requiring the listing of five or seven items of penal nomenclature;
translations.idiomatic: Students of case adjudication were tested on one case, each requiring five or seven items of penal nomenclature to be set forth.

sentences.zh: 習律令，則試大義五道，中格乃得給食。

translations.literal: Those studying statutes and ordinances were examined on five general-principle questions; only after passing the standard were rations granted.
translations.idiomatic: Students of statutes and ordinances faced five general-principle questions; rations were granted only after they met the passing standard.

sentences.zh: 各以所習，月一公試、三私試，略如補試法。

translations.literal: According to what each studied, there was one public examination and three private examinations monthly, broadly following the replenishment-examination method.
translations.idiomatic: Each track held one public and three private examinations monthly, broadly following replenishment-exam practice.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷有新頒條令，刑部即送學。

translations.literal: Whenever the court newly promulgated articles and ordinances, the Ministry of Justice immediately sent them to the school.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court promulgated new statutes, the Ministry of Justice forwarded them to the school at once.

sentences.zh: 其犯降舍殿試者，薄罰金以示辱，餘用太學規矩，而命官聽出宿。

translations.literal: Those who incurred demotion in hall and palace examination received light fines as disgrace; otherwise Imperial College regulations applied, and appointed officials were permitted to lodge outside.
translations.idiomatic: Students demoted in hall rank or palace examination paid modest fines as a mark of disgrace; otherwise Imperial College rules applied, and appointed officials were allowed to lodge off campus.

sentences.zh: 尋又置學正一員，有明法應格而守選者，特免試注官，使兼之，月奉視所授官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward one school rectifier was also established; those qualified in Clear Law who were awaiting selection were specially exempted from examination and appointed to office, serving concurrently, with monthly salary according to the office granted.
translations.idiomatic: A school rectifier was soon added. Candidates qualified in Clear Law who awaited appointment were exempted from further examination, appointed to office, and allowed to serve concurrently at the monthly salary of the post granted.

sentences.zh: 後以教授一員兼管幹本學規矩，仍從太學例給晚食。

translations.literal: Later one instructor concurrently managed the regulations of this school, still receiving evening rations according to Imperial College precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Later one instructor was also assigned to enforce the school’s regulations, still receiving evening rations under Imperial College precedent.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，用國子司業朱服言，命官在學，如公試律義、斷案俱優，準吏部試法授官；

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, following the memorial of Vice Director of the Directorate Zhu Fu, appointed officials in the school who were superior in both public examination on legal principles and case adjudication received office according to the Ministry of Personnel examination method;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, following Vice Director Zhu Fu’s memorial, appointed officials enrolled in the school who excelled in both public exams on legal principles and case adjudication received appointment under Ministry of Personnel examination rules.

sentences.zh: 太學生能兼習律學，中公試第一，比私試第二等。

translations.literal: Imperial College students who could also study law and placed first in the public examination were ranked equal to second grade in the private examination.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial College students who also studied law and placed first on the public exam were credited with second grade on the private exam.

sentences.zh: 政和間，詔博士、學正依大理寺官除授，不許用無出身人及以恩例陳請。

translations.literal: Between the Zhenghe period, an edict ordered that erudites and school rectifiers be appointed like officials of the Court of Judicial Review, and that persons without examination credentials or seeking appointment by grace precedent were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe period, an edict required that erudites and school rectifiers be appointed like Court of Judicial Review officials, barring candidates without examination credentials or those seeking appointment by grace precedent.

sentences.zh: 生徒犯罰者，依學規；

translations.literal: Students who incurred penalties were handled according to school regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Students who violated regulations were punished under school rules;

sentences.zh: 仍犯不改，書其印曆或補牒，參選則理為闕失。

translations.literal: if they offended again without reform, it was entered on their seal register or replenishment certificate, and at selection it was treated as a deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: repeat offenders had the offense recorded on their seal register or replenishment certificate, and at appointment it counted as a disqualifying flaw.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，復明法新科，進士預薦者聽試。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, the Clear Law new category was restored; presented scholars who had been recommended were permitted to sit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3, the new Clear Law category was restored; recommended presented scholars were allowed to take the exam.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，復刑法科。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, the Penal Law category was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1, the Penal Law examination category was restored.

sentences.zh: 凡問題，號為假案，其合格分數，以五十五通分作十分，以所通定分數，以分數定等級：五分以上入第二等下，四分半以上入第三等上，四分以上入第三等中。

translations.literal: For all questions, styled mock cases, the passing score divided fifty-five correct answers into ten parts; the number passed fixed the score, and the score fixed the grade: five parts or above entered lower second grade, four and a half parts or above entered upper third grade, four parts or above entered middle third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Exam questions, styled mock cases, used a fifty-five-point scale converted to ten parts; the number of correct answers determined the score and the score the grade: five parts or more placed in lower second grade, four and a half or more in upper third grade, four or more in middle third grade.

sentences.zh: 以曾經試法人為考官。

translations.literal: Those who had previously passed the legal examination served as examiners.
translations.idiomatic: Examiners were drawn from candidates who had previously passed the legal examination.

sentences.zh: 五年，以李洪嘗中刑法入第二等，命與改秩，中書駁之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Li Hong had passed the penal examination in second grade, an order was issued to promote his rank; the Secretariat rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Li Hong, having passed the penal examination in second grade, was ordered promoted in rank; the Secretariat rejected the order.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎謂：「古者以刑弼教，所宜崇獎。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said: "In antiquity penal law assisted instruction; it should be honored and rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding argued: "In antiquity penal law supported moral instruction; it deserves honor and reward."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「刑名之學久廢，不有以優之，則其學絕矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "The study of penal nomenclature has long been abandoned; unless it is specially favored, that learning will die out."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong replied: "Penal nomenclature has long been neglected; unless we favor it, the discipline will die out."

sentences.zh: 卒如前詔。

translations.literal: In the end it followed the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier edict stood.

sentences.zh: 後議者謂得解人取應，更不兼經，白身得官，反易於有官試法。

translations.literal: Later critics said that presented scholars taking the examination, no longer combining the classics, received office as commoners, which was in fact easier than the legal examination for those already holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Critics later noted that presented scholars sitting the exam without combining the classics could receive office from commoner status—easier, in practice, than the legal exam for officials already in service.

sentences.zh: 乃命所試斷案、刑名，全通及粗通以十分為率，斷及五分、《刑統》義文理全通為合格，及雖全通而斷案不及分數者勿取。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was ordered that in the examination of case adjudication and penal nomenclature, taking full pass and rough pass together at a rate of ten parts, case adjudication reaching five parts and full mastery of the principles of the Penal Code counted as qualified, and that those fully passing in principles but falling short in case adjudication were not to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ruled that on a ten-part scale combining full and rough passes, candidates needed five parts on case adjudication and full mastery of the principles of the Penal Code to qualify; those strong on principles but weak on cases were rejected.

sentences.zh: 仍自後舉兼經。

translations.literal: From later examinations the classics were again combined.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent examinations again required the classics.

sentences.zh: 十五年，罷明法科，以其額歸進士，惟刑法科如舊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the Clear Law category was abolished and its quota returned to the presented scholar category; only the Penal Law category remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, the Clear Law category was abolished and its quota folded into the presented scholar examination; only the Penal Law category remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，四川類省始附試刑法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the Sichuan regional provincial examination first attached the penal examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the Sichuan regional provincial exam first included the penal law examination.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年，秘書郎李巘言：「漢世儀、律、令同藏於理官，而決疑獄者必傅以古義。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunxi, Secretariat Gentleman Li Yan said: "In Han times ritual, law, and ordinances were stored together in the office of the judge, and those deciding doubtful cases always applied ancient principles.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 7, Secretariat Gentleman Li Yan observed: "In Han times ritual, law, and ordinances were kept together in the judge’s office, and doubtful cases were decided by appeal to ancient principle.

sentences.zh: 本朝命學究兼習律令，而廢明法科；

translations.literal: Our dynasty ordered classicists also to study statutes and ordinances, yet abolished the Clear Law category;
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty required classicists to study statutes and ordinances, yet abolished the Clear Law category;

sentences.zh: 後復明法，而以三小經附。

translations.literal: later Clear Law was restored, but with the three minor classics attached.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Law was later restored, but only with the three minor classics attached.

sentences.zh: 蓋欲使經生明法，法吏通經。

translations.literal: The intent was to make classicists understand law and legal clerks master the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to make classicists understand law and legal clerks know the classics.

sentences.zh: 今所試止於斷案、律義，斷案稍通、律義雖不成文，亦得中選，故法官罕能知書。

translations.literal: Now the examination is limited to case adjudication and legal principles; if case adjudication is roughly passed and legal principles, though not fully written out, still allow selection, hence judges rarely know books.
translations.idiomatic: Today the exam tests only case adjudication and legal principles. Rough competence in cases suffices even when principles are poorly written, so successful candidates rarely read widely—and judges seldom know books.

sentences.zh: 宜令習大法者兼習經義，參考優劣。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order those studying major law also to study classic principles, comparing excellence and inferiority."
translations.idiomatic: Candidates studying major law should also be tested on classic principles, with both weighed in ranking."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古之儒者，以儒術決獄，若用俗吏，必流於刻。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Confucians of antiquity decided cases by Confucian learning; if vulgar clerks were used, it would inevitably slide into harshness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Ancient Confucians decided cases through Confucian learning; vulgar clerks would inevitably grow harsh."

sentences.zh: 乃從其奏，詔自今第一、第二、第三場試斷案，每場各三道，第四場大經義一道，小經義二道，第五場《刑統》律義五道。

translations.literal: Thereupon his memorial was followed, and an edict ordered that from now on the first, second, and third sessions examine case adjudication, three questions each session; the fourth session one major classic principle and two minor classic principles; the fifth session five questions on the principles of the Penal Code.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal. An edict ordered three case-adjudication sessions of three questions each; a fourth session with one major and two minor classic principles; and a fifth with five questions on the principles of the Penal Code.

sentences.zh: 明年，命斷案三場，每場止試一道，每道刑名十件，與經義通取，四十分以上為合格，經義定去留，律義定高下。

translations.literal: The next year, case adjudication was set at three sessions, one question per session, ten items of penal nomenclature per question; classic principles and cases were passed together, forty parts or above counted as qualified, classic principles decided retention or rejection, and legal principles decided rank high or low.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the format changed: three case sessions with one question each, ten penal items per question. Classic principles and cases were judged together; forty parts or more qualified, classic principles decided pass or fail, and legal principles determined rank.

sentences.zh: 寧宗慶元三年，以議臣言罷經義，五年又復。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingyuan under Emperor Ningzong, classic principles were abolished on memorialists’ advice; in the fifth year they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 3, memorialists persuaded Emperor Ningzong to drop classic principles; in the fifth year they were restored.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，臣僚上言：「試法設科，本以六場引試，後始增經義一場，而止試五場，律義又居其一，斷案止三場而已，殊失設科之初意。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading, officials memorialized: "The legal examination category was originally established with six sessions of examination; later one session of classic principles was added, yet only five sessions were tested, legal principles occupying one of them and case adjudication only three sessions—greatly departing from the original intent of establishing the category.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 2, officials memorialized: "The legal exam was originally six sessions; later a classic-principles session was added, yet only five were tested—legal principles taking one and case adjudication only three—far from the category’s original purpose.

sentences.zh: 且考試類多文士，輕視法家，惟以經義定去留，其弊一也。

translations.literal: Moreover, examinees are mostly literary men who look down on legalists; retention and rejection are decided only by classic principles—the first abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Most examinees are literary men who despise legal studies; pass and fail hinge on classic principles alone—that is the first abuse.

sentences.zh: 法科欲明憲章，習法令，察舉明比附之精微，識比折出入之錯綜，酌情法於數字之內，決是非於片言之間。

translations.literal: The legal category seeks to clarify statutes, study ordinances, examine the subtlety of analogical application, recognize the complexity of weighing inclusion and exclusion, adjust statutory principle within numbers, and decide right and wrong in the space of a few words.
translations.idiomatic: The legal exam should clarify statutes, train candidates in ordinances, test subtle analogical reasoning, weigh inclusion and exclusion, apply statutory principle within precise numerical rules, and decide right and wrong in a few words.

sentences.zh: 比年案題字多，專尚困人，一日之內，僅能謄寫題目，豈暇深究法意，其弊二也。

translations.literal: In recent years case topics have been wordy, deliberately designed to trap people; within one day one can barely copy out the question, with no leisure to probe legal meaning—the second abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Recently case topics have grown wordy and deliberately trap candidates; in one day they can barely copy the question, let alone grasp legal meaning—the second abuse.

sentences.zh: 刑法考官不過曾中法科丞、評數人，由是請托之風盛，換易之弊興，其弊三也。

translations.literal: Penal law examiners were no more than a few who had passed the legal category as vice directors and reviewers; hence solicitation flourished and substitution abuses arose—the third abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Penal examiners numbered only a few vice directors and reviewers who had passed the legal category—so solicitation flourished and paper substitution became common, the third abuse.

sentences.zh: 今請罷去經義，仍分六場，以五場斷案，一場律義為定。

translations.literal: We now ask to abolish classic principles and again divide six sessions, fixing five sessions of case adjudication and one session of legal principles.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to abolish classic principles and restore six sessions: five on case adjudication and one on legal principles.

sentences.zh: 問題稍減字數，而求精於法律者為試官，各供五六題，納監試或主文臨時點定。

translations.literal: Questions should slightly reduce word count, while examiners skilled in law each supply five or six topics, submitted to the supervising examiner or chief examiner for selection on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Questions should be shorter; skilled legal examiners should each submit five or six topics for the supervising or chief examiner to select on the spot.

sentences.zh: 如是，讞議得人矣。」

translations.literal: If so, judicial deliberation will obtain the right men."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the court would obtain worthy men for judicial deliberation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 六年，以議者言法科止試《刑統》，是盡廢理義而專事法律，遂命復用經義一場，以《尚書》、《語》、《孟》題各一篇及《刑統》大義，通為五場。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because critics said the legal category tested only the Penal Code, wholly abandoning principles and specializing in law alone, an order was issued to restore one session of classic principles, with one essay each from the Book of Documents, the Analects, and the Mencius plus general principles of the Penal Code, five sessions in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, critics argued that testing only the Penal Code abandoned principles for bare law; the court restored one classic-principles session—one essay each from the Book of Documents, the Analects, and the Mencius, plus Penal Code principles—for five sessions total.

sentences.zh: 所出經題，不必拘刑名倫類，以防預備，以斷案定去留，經義為高下，仍禁雜流入貲人收試。

translations.literal: Classic topics issued need not be confined to penal categories and human relations, to guard against advance preparation; case adjudication decided retention and rejection, classic principles decided rank high and low, and miscellaneous-status persons purchasing entry were still forbidden from sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Classic topics need not concern penal categories or human relations, to prevent cramming. Cases decided pass or fail, classic principles determined rank, and miscellaneous-status purchasers were still barred from sitting.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷四川類試刑法科。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Sichuan regional penal examination category was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the Sichuan regional penal law exam was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，凡試法科者，皆取撰成見義挾入試場。

translations.literal: At first, all who took the legal examination brought precomposed prepared essays into the examination hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first, legal examinees smuggled prewritten essays into the examination hall.

sentences.zh: 理宗淳祐三年，令刑部措置關防，其考試則選差大理丞、正曆任中外有聲望者，不許止用新科評事未經作縣之人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunyou under Emperor Lizong, the Ministry of Justice was ordered to arrange safeguards; for the examination, Court of Judicial Review vice directors and directors with established reputations in central and local service were selected and dispatched, and it was not permitted to use only new-category reviewers who had not yet served as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 3, Emperor Lizong ordered the Ministry of Justice to tighten safeguards. Examiners were selected from Court of Judicial Review vice directors and directors of established reputation in central and local service—not merely new-category reviewers who had never served as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 逮其試中，又當仿省試、中書覆試之法，質以疑獄，觀其讞筆明允，始與差除。

translations.literal: When they passed the examination, they should also follow the methods of the provincial examination and Secretariat re-examination, questioning them on doubtful cases and observing whether their judicial drafts were clear and fair before appointment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Successful candidates were also to face provincial-style and Secretariat re-examination: questioned on doubtful cases, their judicial drafts examined for clarity and fairness, before appointment.

sentences.zh: 時所立等第，文法俱通者為上，徑除評事；
